# Agent anatomy

Start with the team in one shared 3D delivery setting: stocked shelves, a packing
bench, loading dock, street and doorstep. Follow a store order from stock check
to picking, dispatch and delivery; recovery evidence then travels to the judge. Click any robot to inspect its parts. The whole
robot stays visible while the component highlights and its explanation appears.
Every hotspot stays available, so you can move directly between parts without
resetting your view. Anatomy is the complete agent reference: all 99 component
panels include **Full reference · read here**, which opens the corresponding
chapter beside the robot. Its section selector and related chapter links keep
reading inside the inspector; **Back to component reference** returns from a
related chapter. **Details & source** exposes the component's policy, evidence,
Agent Card where applicable, and source dialogs.

On a first visit, a skippable four-part tour explains the job, tools, guardrails
and recorded tests. Completion or dismissal is remembered in localStorage;
**Replay tour** starts it again. Reduced motion uses manual **Next** steps.
Selecting a part stops the tour, and **Back to team** returns to the order story.

**View options** contains **Reset view**, **Pause motion**, **Read guide** and
**Chapters**. Guide and chapter navigation remain optional: every selected
component still has its complete reference in the inspector.

The robot is an illustration of code, not a live actor or activity meter. Its
cab, tank, engine, arms and other parts map to the same manifest-backed panels.
The local Three.js renderer uses authored geometry, studio lighting and shadows;
there are no external models or network asset requests. **Pause motion** stops
the idle animation. Reduced motion disables idle movement and handoff animation. Hidden views
stop rendering, and leaving the chapter disposes the scene.

Keyboard users can Tab through component controls, use arrows between them,
and activate with Enter or Space. On the focused 3D canvas, arrows rotate and
plus/minus zoom within bounds that keep the body visible. A native component selector provides the same information.
If WebGL is unavailable or loses its context, the labelled SVG machine remains
fully usable. On a phone, the model stays above the selected component's details.
The desktop reading column keeps the same width for every component, so opening
or closing it never shifts the machine. It scrolls independently on desktop and
uses normal page flow on mobile. The physical part name leads each panel,
followed by its code topic and a plain-language explanation. Each component then leads with a real configuration or evidence number and short
plain-language bullets. Technical numbers, readable result tables and formatted
Agent Cards sit inside **Details & source**; memory retains its visual explorer. Selecting
a memory tab or reading a chapter preserves the chosen camera view.

Local Oxanium headings echo the machine's geometric form. The rest of the page
keeps IBM Plex text and numeric evidence; the shared UI typography is unchanged.
Font attribution and license are in web/fonts/README.md.

## What is technically hard

Keeping a believable agent inside a reliable system is the central problem.
Concurrent stock reservations must not oversell. A retried event must not deliver
or refund twice. A kitchen cannot cook an ingredient that has merely been promised.
A courier going offline mid-delivery must preserve physical custody. Memory must
help the current order without leaking another role's observations.

The design combines granular ADK tools, durable queue transactions, immutable run
definitions, scoped SQL identities, and A2A commands that carry work references.
The agents propose actions; tool implementations enforce the business facts.
SOUL text, retrieved context and incoming messages never grant permissions.

## Reading the machines

The cab explains the mission; the face explains persona; the arms expose tools.
The tank holds scoped memory. The cage explains guardrails, the gauge shows
budgets, and the engine shows deterministic versus model-backed decisions. The
antenna explains A2A and the separate read-only MCP server. Intake and exhaust
show event topics. The inspection sticker shows evidence; the wheels explain
where the code runs.

Each role has a stable purpose color on its body and top light, plus a distinct
symbol. The same color and symbol appear in the named role buttons and the
full-size inspector. Color is never the only identifier. A white ring marks the
current step's owner without changing that role's identity.

The team story is an **illustration, not live traffic**. A demo input creates
a dark-store order; the household robot models meal customers separately. A floor route connects physical handoffs; a raised dashed link shows the
controller-routed A2A request. Dotted review evidence leaves the delivered parcel
at the doorstep. **How agents communicate** explains the protocol legend. The judge reviews recovery decisions,
rather than approving every successful delivery. **Play order** runs one finite
journey; reduced motion offers **Next step** instead. On phones a single scene overview sits above six manual steps and nine named
role buttons. Meal-specific agents and customer service have their own stations
and remain inspectable alongside the main store flow. On the scene canvas,
arrows orbit and Home resets the viewpoint. Every role is also keyboard-accessible
through its named button; **Back to team** restores focus to that role.

The shared scene reuses a lower-detail version of the inspector's robot geometry.
It renders only when visible and changed, caps its render rate at 30 frames per
second and pixel ratio at 1.3, and disposes resources when leaving the chapter.
If 3D fails, a grouped floor plan retains all roles and manual story controls.
The inspector keeps its separate labelled SVG fallback.

The cab badge shows the role, and arm symbols represent up to four of that
role's actual tools. The gauge compares default USD model spending caps across
these templates: dark bars mean a zero default model budget, not an exhausted
balance. Customer service's default is $0.02 per run; optional ADK and cloud
profiles have their own limits. The inspector identifies the unit and scope.

## Inspecting memory

Select the storage tank to inspect the exact stored format, what reaches the
agent core, the local and optional Google Cloud paths, and their constraints.
The examples are explicitly synthetic. The page reads no private run memory,
database, deployment status or provider, and changing a preview changes no run.

**Record** shows PostgreSQL rows with a JSONB body, rather than a CSV, chat
transcript or file per agent. Select **Scope**, **Observation** or **History** to
see the corresponding fields. The body is selected initially; roles with several
observation kinds expose an **Observation type** selector. **Accepted body
schema** and **Complete example record** expose the full schema and record.
Examples are validated with the same role-specific Python contracts as the
runtime. Scope comes from the authenticated role and leased event; identity,
revision and provenance come from SQL. Times are simulation seconds.

**Core view** projects that same example through the real projection function:

| Profile | What reaches the core |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | An empty list; writes and audit history still exist. |
| `text` | A bounded string containing scope, facts and provenance. |
| `json` | A JSON object separating shared scope, fact bodies and provenance. |
| `typed` | Complete typed records with scope and provenance. |
| `semantic` | Typed records after ranking permitted candidates; the one-record preview demonstrates shape, not measured search quality. |

The recall diagram follows the leased event through the SQL scope gate, optional
ranking, SQL recheck and agent input. Restaurant ADK receives the selected
projection in its tool response. Deterministic workers use canonical facts for
decisions and audit; selecting a memory profile adds no model. The packaged
local embedding model makes no paid embedding API calls. SQL still rechecks
scope, lease, expiry and revision after ranking.

**Local / GCP** separates canonical records from their optional search index.
Locally, Docker Compose retains PostgreSQL data in `postgres-data`;
`agent_memory_facts` stores the observations, and `agent_semantic_vectors` holds
embedding arrays used by optional pgvector search. On Google Cloud, the
implemented Terraform path uses Cloud Run workers and Cloud SQL/PostgreSQL 17,
with optional Vertex Vector Search. The Vertex payload contains vectors, fact
IDs, scope/model hashes and expiry metadata, without raw fact text. Hashes are
filters, not encryption, and embeddings remain derived data.

The cloud view describes prerequisites rather than claiming a live deployment:
`active` and `enable_live` enable live storage, `live_ready` follows migration,
login and secret setup, and `enable_vector_search` adds Vertex. Authenticated
public API calls and scoped service-account grants govern access. Cloud SQL and
the one-replica Vertex deployment incur idle costs. The current lab disables SQL
backups and deletion protection; teardown can remove retained history. No
automatic Vertex TTL deletion or archival pipeline is implemented.

**Constraints** distinguishes recall budgets from storage capacity. An explicit
profile defaults to eight complete facts, 8,192 UTF-8 bytes and a 3,600-second
simulation lifetime; allowed bounds come from the profile schema. Per-role live
entry, body-byte and tool limits come from its manifest. An unset profile keeps
legacy recall behavior, not an implied explicit profile. Oversized facts are
omitted whole. Writes are idempotent for the same source event/type/subject;
conflicting content is rejected. Every recall uses a tool slot, and semantic
recall uses two fenced reads.

The lifecycle shows why expiry does not erase the audit trail or revive an older
revision. A disabled recall profile also preserves writes and audit history.
Scope prevents cross-order and cross-role recall; SQL functions and grants
enforce access, while the Python host and operator remain trusted. Observations
provide context, never new authority or proof that an observation is true.

Customer-service classification has a different, explicit view: a fresh ADK
session for each complaint, no persistent memory contract and no memory tools.
Durable request/result receipts prevent repeat billing; they are not recall.
Its separate Chaos turn receives only the affected order facts. A disclosure
explains the shared storage system without presenting it as a classifier feature.

Use Left/Right or Home/End within the four-tab list, or click a tab. The memory
chapter, source files and related references remain available in the same
inspector. The reference distinguishes local embedding/pgvector tests and mocked
Vertex request tests from a live GCP quality benchmark; no memory-specific
production pass rate, latency or monetary cost receipt is claimed.

## One authority, several profiles

Each repository-owned `role.json` is the capability ceiling. The published
[JSON Schema](../config/agents/role.schema.json) comes from the same Pydantic model
used to validate the files. A run snapshot can remove capabilities, never add
them. Restaurant tool profiles, main-service queue events and Chaos recovery
tools are declared in those same manifests. Fixed SQL and Python implementations
still enforce what each operation means; adding a string does not create a tool.

The restaurant has deterministic and ADK profiles, and the recovery judge has an
optional GCP profile. Customer-service classification is ADK with **no business
tools**; its separate Chaos turn has bounded recovery tools. Supply definitions
may choose a different SOUL or tighter budget and freeze it for that run. The
anatomy page describes checked-in templates, not private live run state.

## What the numbers prove

The [held-out release summary](evidence/heldout-release.json) records six offline
ADK arms, 72 cases and five attempts per case. pass^k counts cases where every
attempt passed. The all-pass bootstrap interval is degenerate; it is not a claim
of certainty on new tasks. Offline $0 cost and millisecond latency are not live
inference performance. Deterministic roles without a held-out ADK arm say so.

The [recorded Chaos shift](evidence/a2a-chaos-local.json) measures 1,148–1,765
**simulated seconds** to recover across five disruptions, with zero lost orders
in those cohorts. This includes delivery completion, not just replanning latency.
Cohorts overlap and do not establish a causal “orders saved” counterfactual.
Its €1.7215 per delivery is synthetic operating cost, not a model bill.

The [main consolidation receipt](evidence/main-consolidation.json) is historical
suite evidence. The current test result belongs to its own verification record;
this page never silently relabels old results as a fresh run.

## How the page stays honest

The [presentation builder](../src/delivery/anatomy_presentation.py) generates
plain labels, human number rows, evidence headlines and the narrated team flow.
The [data builder](../src/delivery/agent_anatomy.py) reads manifests and SOUL files,
uses the real Agent Card factory, inspects MCP declarations and loads dated eval
receipts. The [memory reference builder](../src/delivery/memory_reference.py)
validates synthetic bodies with the runtime contracts and generates all five
projections using the real memory profile function. It does not connect to a
database or provider. The browser renders the supplied facts and examples;
it does not maintain a second fact catalogue. A fingerprint covers
all source inputs, and contract tests compare panels, permissions, cards, event
edges, evidence and the published schema against their originating files.

The component readers include [agent implementation](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md),
[ADK restaurants](ADK-RESTAURANT.md), [memory](AGENT-MEMORY.md),
[A2A](A2A.md), and [evaluations](AGENT-EVALS.md). Related chapter links inside a
component reader stay beside the robot; source links open inspectable dialogs.

pages.body:
# Architecture overview

This project is a local engineering environment for studying bounded agent work:
ingredient sourcing, stock reservations, consent, courier assignment, physical
delivery and recovery. Its reusable runtime combines authenticated Python workers
with PostgreSQL transactions. Most decisions use fixed rules. A separately enabled
GCP recovery judge complements Google ADK restaurant and customer-service adapters.
Both ADK roles have scripted, zero-network models for CI. The dispatcher and
customer service are discoverable over local A2A; optional OTel spans and
BigQuery exports connect decisions to operational evidence.

This chapter describes source reviewed on **2026-10-29**. It does not report a new
deployment or a current cloud inventory. Read [capability evidence](CAPABILITY-EVIDENCE.md)
for measured limits and [architecture decisions](ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md) for
the alternatives behind these choices.

## Three boundaries

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Local["Local Docker environment"]
        Operator["Operator UI and trusted controller"]
        World["Synthetic city and physical world engine"]
        Workers["Scoped Python LocalAgent workers"]
        DB[("PostgreSQL: domain state, queue, memory, budgets and audit")]
        Client["Optional CloudJudge client"]
        Operator --> Workers
        Operator --> World
        World <--> DB
        Workers <--> DB
        Workers -->|"Explicit GCP judge mode"| Client
    end
    subgraph Cloud["Optional Terraform-owned GCP resources"]
        IAM["Cloud Run IAM: caller identity"]
        Gateway["Cloud Run judgement container"]
        Model["Google publisher model through Vertex REST"]
        Image["Artifact Registry: immutable image digest"]
        Logs["Platform logs and structured gateway stdout"]
        IAM --> Gateway
        Image -.-> Gateway
        Gateway -->|"Runtime service account ADC"| Model
        Gateway --> Logs
    end
    Client -->|"HTTPS and audience-bound ID token"| IAM
    Gateway -->|"Validated verdict and usage"| Client
```

The **city boundary** owns virtual time, directed roads, congestion, courier
movement and recorded arrival. Agents request permitted transitions; they cannot
manufacture physical arrival. The **agent boundary** owns scoped observations,
approved tools, leased work and bounded recall. PostgreSQL is the authority for
stock, consent, custody and execution. Redis supports the local baseline but is
not the authoritative agent transport.

The **cloud boundary** accepts a bounded numeric recovery proposal and returns an
approve/deny verdict. It has no simulation database connection or execution tools.
Caller and runtime service accounts have separate duties. Cloud Run is reachable
over the public network with IAM-authenticated invocation; the Terraform module
does not provide private ingress. Cloud SQL, Pub/Sub, GKE, managed Agent
Runtime and Memory Bank are not deployed. Google ADK runs as a local Python
library; optional Cloud Trace and BigQuery resources are declared but parked.
See the [Google stack guide](GOOGLE-STACK.md) and
[exact GCP inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md).

## What an agent actually is

`create_agent` produces the same frozen `LocalAgent` class for inventory,
fulfillment, dispatch, couriers, the recovery judge and supply entities. Its
inputs resolve to an authenticated scope, validated `RoleSpec`, definition hash
and restricted database connection. The public loop is `claim()` followed by
`process(event)`. Role-specific policies decide through `ScopedTools`; the factory
does not generate a new program for each fictional participant.

A trusted controller provisions the login and freezes the definition. SQL derives
scope from the authenticated database identity. Server-owned authority limits
tools, accepted topics and recipients. Editable names and SOUL text describe the
role; current deterministic policies do not interpret SOUL. Business settings
such as stock, opening hours, latency and numeric limits have implemented effects.
New roles still require code, database permissions and tests. The complete
[agent construction walkthrough](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md) follows these steps.

For one event, an attempt/tool reservation commits first. The effects transaction
then validates the lease and authoritative payload, reads domain state and typed
recall, executes allowed actions, records the decision and outgoing events, and
ACKs. Those effects commit together or roll back together. Durable reservations
survive failure. This protects business effects without promising exactly-once
external inference or billing. Sources: [runtime](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py),
[queue](../src/delivery/queue.py), [identity provisioning](../src/delivery/agent_access.py).

## Follow one household pizza request

This is a representative path with a pantry shortage, not a promise that every
seed follows it. Role handoffs use typed queued events; notes and self-steps
describe domain work.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Household agent
    participant R as Restaurant agent
    participant M as Market agent
    participant D as Dispatcher
    participant C as Courier agent
    participant W as Physical world
    H->>R: household.call for pizza
    R->>M: market.request for missing ingredient
    Note over M: Reserve own stock or forward to an unvisited market
    M->>R: ingredient.arrived after transfer
    Note over H,R: A replacement requires explicit household approval
    Note over R: Cook only from arrived, reserved ingredients
    R->>D: basket.ready
    D->>C: courier.briefed
    C->>D: courier.accepted
    W->>D: delivery.arrived after road traversal
    D->>D: dispatch.complete records delivered status
    H->>H: meal.delivery checks canonical job status
```

The restaurant first checks menu, availability and pantry. Markets reserve
unreserved quantities atomically, or forward shortages through a bounded visited
list. A promised ingredient is unusable until arrival commits. A substitution
must satisfy the fixed rules, household exclusions and recorded consent before
cooking consumes the physical allocations once.

Cooking creates a delivery job and a dispatcher handoff. The courier must accept
its own briefing before departure; the world advances it along directed edges.
Ingredient transfer uses scheduled transitions rather than a separate moving
supplier vehicle. The restaurant-to-courier handoff **is implemented**; it is
covered by [delivery-fact regressions](../tests/test_supply_delivery_facts.py).

## Observability trace flow

Observability is disabled by default. One run-scoped order trace continues across
durable queue handoffs and lease retries. Explicit agent, ADK model and tool spans
record names, usage and estimated cost; FastAPI and Redis use OpenTelemetry
instrumentors. Exporters remove payloads and exception text before sending data.

The [Mermaid trace-flow diagram](ARCHITECTURE-OBSERVABILITY.md#trace-flow) follows
the API, persisted queue context, agent/tool spans and both export paths.

Trace and analytics flags are independent. Analytics outages do not change task
outcomes; Postgres and local receipts remain authoritative. The four BigQuery
tables have daily partitions, agent clustering and bounded retention. Saved SQL
deduplicates streaming rows before calculating cost per successful task, p95 tool
latency and eval pass^k trends. See [setup, privacy, reporting limits and
retention](ARCHITECTURE-OBSERVABILITY.md).

## Distinct workspaces and reading paths

The [restaurant workflow](RESTAURANT-SUPPLY.md) starts with household meal demand,
sourcing and consent, then reuses fleet delivery. The [delivery lab](FLEET-RECOVERY.md)
starts with stocked baskets and concentrates on fulfillment, contention, traffic,
dropouts and checkpoint recovery. They share infrastructure and some roles, but
their seeded scenarios and success criteria differ. The [inventory lab](AGENT-FOUNDATION.md)
isolates last-unit contention, delayed supply and worker crashes.

For a demonstration, open one restaurant order and inspect its call, ingredient
requests, actual memory revisions, queue lineage, cooking and physical handoff.
Then use a delivery-lab failure to inspect custody and the judge's limited
authority. Compare those observations with [local scenario evaluations](AGENT-EVALS.md).

For implementation, continue through [agent internals](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md),
[memory](AGENT-MEMORY.md) and [GCP components](GCP-COMPONENTS.md). For a client or
interview discussion, use the [decision records](ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md) and
[enterprise roadmap](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md). [Durable inference](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md)
now saves requests/results and invokes outside SQL connections, with local crash
verification. Controller recovery, workload identity, retention and measured
production release gates remain proposed work.

# Shelf to doorstep

Open Operations and choose **Start store demo**. One seeded synthetic order is
reserved from the catalogue, picked from physical shelves, packed, carried to the
loading dock, then delivered by a Madrid courier. **Picker breakdown** adds a
failure while the basket is in progress. The 60-second playback setting is a
target; a slower machine will take longer rather than skip physical steps.

The default view is an elevated cutaway. Cyan marks the selected order's shelf
faces and the current planned route. Green items are already in the basket.
Amber blocks show inaccessible cells. Use **Track worker** for a closer camera,
**Fit store** for the whole layout, or **Back to Madrid** to leave. **Follow this
order** returns to the city after physical courier collection; it ends at delivery
or cancellation. Select a robot or forklift label to follow that worker; the label
shows its actual task and the ground marker follows its route. Completed shifts
are labeled **shift complete**; start a store demo for live movement. Escape
leaves the store. On a focused 3D view, arrows orbit and
plus/minus zoom. All order facts and controls remain available without WebGL.

## Two environments, one order

`Environment` defines clock reads, ordered events, state reads and transactional
advance effects. `MadridCity` contains the original city physics; city-only runs
retain their minute tick and behavior. `DarkStore` shares its run ID and clock,
advances physical movement every ten simulated seconds, and records store frames.

`StoreLayoutConfig` generates four aisles, eight bays, three shelf levels, a cold
zone, a packing station and a loading dock by default. The sixty supermarket
catalogue products have two distinct pick faces each, including cold storage for
dairy, protein and frozen items. Opening physical stock is 24 units per SKU;
listing a product or expecting a truck never creates sellable stock.

Stock models sit inside the actual rack bounds on its raycast deck surfaces;
logical levels select usable decks rather than placing goods in mid-air. Shelf
and product instances share draw calls.

The renderer uses metre coordinates from this layout, not a separate visual
layout. Pick routes use deterministic shortest aisle paths, avoid rack cells and
blocked cells, and pick ambient goods before cold goods. This is a discrete
logistics simulation; it is not collision-accurate robotics physics. Worker
traffic does not yet reserve space against other workers.

## Agent decisions and bounded effects

The inventory role reuses `InventoryPolicy`, its typed reservation outcomes and
memory validation. A bound adapter permits only the selected run, store and
order. The fulfillment role adds a dark-store tool profile: route, pick, pack,
restock and handoff. Its policy observes available faces, workers and routes.
It does not branch on incident names. Both roles expose Agent Cards and execute
through the same A2A service used by the in-process test transport.

A route is only a plan. The environment emits an arrival event; a scoped tool
then checks reservation, quantity, position and elapsed time before changing
stock. A replacement picker must reach a broken robot before taking its basket.
The forklift first visits the dock and moves only confirmed backstock. Pack and
handoff tools refuse incomplete baskets. The dispatcher cannot assign an order
until the dock is ready.

Each decision is in the existing event/decision trail, with the same order ID.
New spans describe tools and environment advances; the observability system is
otherwise unchanged. The local policies use no model calls. The optional GCP
configuration includes separate inventory and fulfillment identities with
audience-bound A2A tokens; no cloud resources are started by this feature.

Store services use trusted database connections and bound application tools.
They do not claim the legacy inventory lab's separate SQL-login isolation.
Manifest profiles limit per-turn tools, per-run work, memory size and TTL.
Stock is conserved through cancellation, receipts, retries and disruptions.

## Store disruptions

| Event | Physical change | Decision left to the policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blocked aisle | Removes cells from the walk graph | Choose another face/path, or wait |
| Shelf out of stock | Removes a pick face; observed units move to unlocated backstock | Pick another face; forklift may restock a reachable face |
| Robot breakdown | Stops a robot at its last safe node | Recover its basket with an available picker |
| Late restock truck | Delays an expected receipt | Wait for actual receipt; never promise expected stock |

The existing Chaos API accepts these event kinds, `target` (a store ID or
`auto`) and optional `resource` (aisle, shelf, robot or shipment ID).
Explicit resources require an explicit store. Scenarios can provide an event
list; `random_store_events` uses a separate seeded stream so existing city
random sequences remain unchanged. Auto targets resolve from current store
load. Store decisions and events remain correlated to their order.

## API and recording

`POST /api/runs` accepts an optional `dark_store` configuration. Omit it for
the unchanged city simulation. `GET /api/runs/{run}/stores` returns current
layout, stock, worker routes, baskets and live load. Add `?at=120` to read the
last recorded frame at or before 120 simulated seconds. This endpoint is read
only and uses a consistent database snapshot.

For a short recording, submit the checked-in demo request:

```bash
curl -fsS http://localhost:8010/api/stores/demo \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @config/scenarios/store-demo.json
```

The UI's demo button makes the same request, selects `DS-0001`, and follows it.
An optional `chaos: true` inserts a robot failure. These are synthetic orders,
not real shoppers or customer communications. Live deployments retain global
authentication on all endpoints; public replay exposes no write APIs.

## Evidence and browser budget

`evals/store/scenarios.json` runs all four incidents twice over the official
A2A SDK. The gate recomputes pass criteria: delivered on time, complete basket,
dock recovery within 900 seconds, conserved stock, no orphan reservations, no
dead events, no paid calls, and identical normalized outcomes across repeats.
Robot recovery must be observed, and delayed trucks cannot be received early.

The seven NVIDIA SimReady models converted by
[codepawl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/codepawl/simready-glb) are
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Derivatives simplify
geometry, resize textures to 256 px, and use WebP and Meshopt compression.
The pinned source revision, original links, modifications and hashes are in
`web/vendor/simready/manifest.json`. The models total 920,992 bytes; models plus
the local Three.js loader stay below 4 MB. They load only when opening a store.
Failed models use boxes; failed WebGL uses the floor plan. Rendering is capped
at 30 fps and pixel ratio 1.5, skips unchanged frames, reduces resolution on slow
software GPUs, pauses in hidden views, and disposes its renderer
when closed. The original model geometry is visual evidence, not the simulation's
physical collision or navigation authority.

## Source index

- [Environment contract](../src/delivery/environment.py)
- [Madrid city adapter](../src/delivery/madrid_city.py)
- [Store layout and navigation](../src/delivery/store_layout.py)
- [Physical store state and effects](../src/delivery/dark_store.py)
- [Scoped store tools](../src/delivery/store_tools.py)
- [Inventory adapter and fulfillment policy](../src/delivery/store_agents.py)
- [Measured recovery runner](../src/delivery/store_evals.py)
- [Frozen store scenarios](../evals/store/scenarios.json)
- [Asset provenance and byte budget](../web/vendor/simready/manifest.json)

# Google stack: demonstrate a decision and its evidence

This portfolio slice connects Google ADK, A2A, OpenTelemetry, and BigQuery to a
working delivery simulator. The core demonstration is free: PostgreSQL owns
state, queue leases, permissions, memory and budgets; scripted ADK models exercise
the real Runner; Jaeger inspects local traces. Cloud features remain separately
enabled and no paid provider is invoked in CI.

## A short technical demonstration

1. Start with `make setup` and open `/architecture`, `/agent-traces`, and `/health`.
2. Run `make demo-adk` to compare scripted restaurant behaviors with stored tool,
   outcome and usage evidence. The fixture measures contract compliance, not LLM quality.
3. Discover both [A2A agents](A2A.md). Call an existing order or complaint with
   the official client and inspect its durable event, outcome, and replay.
4. Enable [local tracing](OBSERVABILITY.md), repeat a run, and follow a trace from
   the queue producer through an agent and its tools into downstream work.
5. [Prepare a BigQuery bundle](GOOGLE-ANALYTICS.md) from the receipt. Inspect the
   allowlisted rows and SQL dashboard view without contacting Google Cloud.

This shows how a customer-facing engineer can move from a business failure
(late delivery, stock contention, courier dropout) to a bounded agent action,
an auditable result, and an operational metric.

## Google ADK customer service

The [customer adapter](../src/delivery/adk_customer.py) replaces the former direct
GenAI call with `LlmAgent`, `Runner`, and `InMemorySessionService`. It uses a strict
Advice schema, no tools or transfers, one model call, no automatic provider
retries, and a bound on the complete serialized request. The existing
[service](../src/delivery/customer_service.py) still admits work through a durable
reservation before invoking the model, reuses cached results, and falls back to
operator review after an error, exhausted budget, or disabled provider.

`LLM_PROVIDER=offline` selects the scripted customer model, which records zero
dollars but still consumes the existing call/token allowance. `disabled` remains
the default outside the explicit local A2A demonstration. Paid `gemini` and
`vertex` modes retain the original call, token and dollar ceilings. The fixed
refund policy remains outside the model; the offline source cannot authorize a
refund. Unknown usage after a provider error retains its full reservation; zero
recorded tokens in an error receipt does not prove zero provider spend.

The [customer tests](../tests/test_adk_customer.py) cover the real offline Runner,
input/schema bounds, one-call enforcement, provider configuration, durable
reservation and replay. [Original safety tests](../tests/test_safety.py) continue
to verify injection handling, the refund gate and concurrent budget admission.

## Interfaces, operations and limits

| Capability | Working path | Cloud boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADK restaurant + customer | Real Runner, scripted model, scoped tools or structured Advice | Explicit Vertex/Gemini configuration; existing budget gates |
| A2A | Two 1.0 JSON-RPC servers, cards and real SDK client | Loopback demonstration; external tenant authentication is not implemented |
| OpenTelemetry | W3C queue propagation and local Jaeger, linked from trace inspector | Explicit collector export, trace-only service account, sampling |
| BigQuery | Local NDJSON receipts/KPIs, frozen manifest, mocked upload tests | Opt-in dataset/tables/view, bounded batch loads, scoped service account |
| Looker Studio | Dashboard-ready BigQuery SQL view and field guide | Connecting a live dashboard is an operator step; query charges are separate |

Existing inference cost caps in [cloud_ai.py](../src/delivery/cloud_ai.py) are
unchanged. Cloud Trace ingestion, BigQuery storage and dashboard queries have
separate service pricing; none are enabled by `make setup`. Infrastructure and
upload tests use mocks, never a live GCP project. Google Maps ETA comparison and
managed Agent Engine deployment remain optional future extensions.

The [public-readiness review](PUBLIC-READINESS.md) records ignored secret/state
files and the history scan. GitHub visibility remains private. The GIF in the
README is explicitly a placeholder, not claimed footage.

## Reproduce the checks

The [local verification receipt](evidence/google-stack-local.json) records 628
passing tests, Ruff, mypy over 54 modules, twelve scenarios repeated twice with
49/49 criteria passing, mocked Terraform checks, and the Jaeger/export smoke test.
It identifies the exact regression revision and distinguishes local evidence
from untested live cloud integration.

```bash
make setup
make check
make test
make eval-agents
docker compose exec -T app pytest -q tests/test_a2a_server.py tests/test_adk_customer.py tests/test_telemetry.py tests/test_bigquery_export.py
python3 scripts/check_documentation.py
```

Run suites using the shared `delivery_test` database sequentially; concurrent
suites can invalidate fixture-cleanup assertions. Terraform checks use an
isolated working directory, a mocked provider, and Terraform 1.14 or newer
(which handles protected resources during mock-test teardown). See each feature
guide for exact cloud opt-in and parking commands. No live Cloud Trace or
BigQuery deployment is claimed by these local checks.

Official API documentation checked on 2026-10-29:

- [ADK agents](https://adk.dev/agents/llm-agents/), [Gemini models](https://adk.dev/agents/models/google-gemini/), and [RunConfig](https://adk.dev/runtime/runconfig/).
- [A2A Python SDK](https://a2aproject.github.io/a2a-python/) and [server routes](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/tutorials/python/5-start-server/).
- [Cloud Trace Python/OTel](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/setup/python-ot).
- [BigQuery local-file loads](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/samples/bigquery-load-from-file) and [IAM permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control).

# Architecture decisions

These records explain the implemented choices reviewed on **2026-10-28** and
when to reconsider them. The local environment supplies reproducible engineering
evidence; it does not establish production scale or superiority over another
agent architecture. [Enterprise GCP](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md) expands the proposed
deployment and governance work.

## 1. Keep the queue and business effects in PostgreSQL

**Choice.** Use addressed events, leases, fencing, priorities, retries and dead
letters beside the domain tables. The worker commits state, memory, decision,
outgoing events and ACK in one effects transaction. Attempt/model reservations
commit separately and survive failure.

**Alternative.** Introduce a message broker as the authoritative work transport.
**Why.** A stock change and its handoff can share a database transaction; a crash
cannot commit consumption while losing its next event. **Trade-off.** Locks and
database capacity constrain execution. Cloud inference now releases its connection
between durable preparation and saved-result application; an uncertain dispatch
fails closed rather than being resent. **Revisit when** measured queue load or independent
consumers justify a broker. Use an outbox/inbox design and failure tests; a broker
does not make external billing exactly once.

Sources: [queue](../src/delivery/queue.py), [runtime](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py),
[queue boundary tests](../tests/test_agent_queue_boundary.py),
[durable request/result protocol](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md).

## 2. Use rules first, with an optional bounded recovery judge

**Choice.** Fixed policies handle inventory, sourcing, consent, routes and custody.
An explicitly enabled GCP judge may veto a locally computed retry candidate.
**Alternative.** Delegate planning and tool choice to an LLM for every role.
**Why.** Exact stock arithmetic and physical feasibility have executable answers;
default runs remain reproducible without paid inference. **Trade-off.** Fixed
policies cannot interpret an unfamiliar instruction or invent a sourcing strategy.
The model's additional business value remains unmeasured. **Revisit when** an
ambiguous task has an approved evidence contract and a held-out comparison shows
better outcomes within quality, latency and cost gates.

Sources: [supply policy](../src/delivery/supply_policy.py),
[fleet policy](../src/delivery/fleet_policy.py),
[veto/failure tests](../tests/test_cloud_runtime.py).

## 3. Enforce scope outside prompts

**Choice.** Bind each worker's run, namespace and role to its PostgreSQL login;
enforce domain operations through RLS, narrow functions, live leases and budgets.
**Alternative.** Give a shared privileged connection to agents and ask them to
respect their prompt's store/order boundaries. **Why.** Model content, recalled
text and display names cannot grant authority. **Trade-off.** Provisioning and
schema migrations carry complexity. Trusted controller, host and fixed Python
remain outside this boundary; one process holding several connections is not an
OS sandbox. **Revisit when** moving to independently deployed or tenant-facing
workers: add workload identity, process isolation and negative authorization tests.

Sources: [access provisioning](../src/delivery/agent_access.py),
[server-owned authority](../src/delivery/agent_specs.py),
[isolation tests](../tests/test_agent_runtime.py).

## 4. Start with typed memory and explicit sharing

**Choice.** Store versioned observations with server-derived provenance, expiry
and role/order/request/attempt filters. Share approved canonical facts in queued
briefs rather than opening another agent's private memory. **Alternative.** Put
all conversations into shared vector recall by default. **Why.** The current task
needs exact context and auditable stale-fact behavior, not semantic similarity.
**Trade-off.** No cross-order learning, automatic consolidation or semantic recall
exists. TTL controls recall eligibility, not audit deletion. **Revisit when** a
held-out retrieval task demonstrates a gap; compare scoped full-text/vector or
managed memory against this baseline with leakage and latency measurements.

Sources: [typed contracts](../src/delivery/typed_memory.py),
[memory SQL](../sql/migrations/015_typed_memory.sql),
[memory regressions](../tests/test_typed_memory.py).

## 5. Reuse a factory and freeze editable definitions

**Choice.** All supported roles use `LocalAgent`; strict definitions and their
hashes are frozen per run. Supply blueprints allow entity overrides and revision
checks. **Alternative.** Create separate frameworks per role or let instructions
modify capabilities at runtime. **Why.** One execution contract makes permissions,
budgets and evidence consistent. **Trade-off.** SOUL is versioned guidance that
deterministic policies do not interpret; editing it cannot add behavior. The GCP
gateway uses a separate fixed prompt and does not receive local SOUL. **Revisit
when** adding a reasoning adapter: deliberately assemble trusted instructions and
bounded observations, retain prompt versions, and preserve independent enforcement.

Sources: [factory](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py),
[supply definitions](../src/delivery/supply_models.py),
[definition tests](../tests/test_supply_models.py),
[gateway prompt](../infra/gcp-ai/gateway.py).

## 6. Host the optional judge on Cloud Run

**Choice.** Deploy a stateless container calling Vertex REST, with separate caller
and runtime service accounts. **Alternative.** Managed Agent Runtime, ADK hosting
or GKE. **Why.** A bounded HTTP verdict fits the existing explicit container,
IAM and Terraform lifecycle. **Trade-off.** Managed sessions, memory, agent
identity and governance are not supplied by this design. Network reachability
is public with authenticated invocation. **Revisit when** client requirements
justify managed lifecycle capabilities or different isolation/network controls.
Evaluate the same task and permissions; a framework object alone does not create
a distinct workload identity.

Sources: [Terraform](../infra/gcp-ai/main.tf),
[cloud client](../src/delivery/cloud_ai.py), [component inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md).

## 7. Keep routine work local and park billable runtime explicitly

**Choice.** Default providers are disabled. Optional GCP resources belong to a
dedicated Terraform project. Daily stop removes Cloud Run, its invoker binding and
Artifact Registry before unlinking billing; project, APIs and IAM remain.
**Alternative.** Always-on cloud infrastructure or deleting/recreating the entire
project each session. **Why.** Local checks need no model account, while retained
identity/project ownership avoids repeated setup. **Trade-off.** Retention and
shutdown need explicit accounting. Six per-run model calls and token reservations
do not create a project-wide dollar cap. **Revisit when** a client needs persistent
services, backups or multi-caller inference; add cost admission and declared
retention/containment ownership.

Sources: [local Compose](../compose.yaml), [lifecycle helper](../scripts/gcp_demo.py),
[lifecycle tests](../tests/test_gcp_demo_commands.py), [operations](GCP-AI.md).

## 8. Publish measured receipts before architecture rankings

**Choice.** Keep source-linked tests, fixed scenario criteria, repeat hashes,
business replay and explicit freshness. **Alternative.** Rank architectures or
models from a convincing animation or one successful run. **Why.** A safe rejection
can be correct; scores require declared expectations and complete measurements.
**Trade-off.** The battery covers development regressions, not generalization,
production SLOs or causal business uplift. **Revisit when** comparing flat,
hierarchical or planner/executor designs: freeze paired incidents, hold out case
families, repeat trials and publish quality, latency, cost and failure outcomes.

Sources: [scenario evaluator](../src/delivery/scenario_evals.py),
[receipt validation](../src/delivery/scenario_report.py),
[reporting tests](../tests/test_scenario_evals.py), [evidence guide](CAPABILITY-EVIDENCE.md).

# Capability evidence

The six goals below connect the architecture to executable proof and its limits.
Source review is dated **2026-10-28**. The dated
[implementation review](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md) records **392 passing tests**.
The role battery declares **12 fixed scenarios and 49 criteria**, with matching
outcomes across two seed-731 repetitions. These are historical development results,
not a current service-health statement or a new test run performed by reading
this chapter. The earlier [local receipt](evidence/local-health.json) records a
different snapshot of 353 tests; it is not the receipt for the 392-test result.
See the [scenario receipt](evidence/agent-scenarios-local.json) and
[evaluation contract](AGENT-EVALS.md).

Tests exercise narrower guarantees than their headlines suggest. Follow the
linked assertions, distinguish successful rejection from business success, and
use the running health view for current source/freshness information.

## 1. Queue resilience

**Goal:** agents must cooperate through durable work and recover safely from
duplicates, contention, stale workers and failure.

**Implemented proof:** the [queue](../src/delivery/queue.py) and
[capability migration](../sql/migrations/014_queue_capability.sql) provide addressed
claims, due times, priority, lease fencing, retries/backoff, deduplication and dead
letters. [Queue tests](../tests/test_queue.py) exercise concurrent claims, rollback,
retry and replay. [Agent boundary tests](../tests/test_agent_queue_boundary.py)
reject raw mutation, forged publication and stale ACKs; they recheck deadlines
after lock waits and verify authoritative payload reload. The fixed battery
includes a real worker-process crash before acknowledgement.

**Limit:** domain effects, memory, decision, outbox and ACK are atomic in the fixed
worker. This does not promise exactly-once inference or billing. Sustained
throughput/backpressure, durable controller restart and orphan-login recovery
remain unmeasured or unfinished. The optional judge now invokes outside database
connections, reuses saved results, and fails closed on uncertain abandoned calls.
[Real process-crash tests](../tests/test_inference_crash_recovery.py) verify those
boundaries without paid inference. [Implementation details](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md).

## 2. Hierarchy, coordination and authority

**Goal:** give cooperating roles different responsibilities and prevent one role
from overruling another's business authority.

**Implemented proof:** the [authority contract](../src/delivery/agent_specs.py)
defines each role's tools and topics. A dispatcher assigns work, a courier accepts
its own brief, a judge reviews recovery, and domain commands independently enforce
consent, stock and custody. [Fleet tests](../tests/test_fleet_recovery.py) cover two
dispatchers competing for one bike, cross-courier denial, mandatory judgement and
checkpoint handoff. [Delivery tests](../tests/test_delivery_flow.py) reject
cross-domain commands and invented physical arrival. A judge's verdict cannot
manufacture a route or move a parcel.

**Limit:** role coordination and approval gates are implemented; a generic
hierarchical planner is not. Flat, hierarchical and planner/executor architecture
comparisons are **not implemented**. Counting roles or showing a handoff does not
measure the value of a hierarchy. The host, operator and fixed policies remain
trusted. [Fleet workflow](FLEET-RECOVERY.md).

## 3. Shared memory without unrestricted access

**Goal:** preserve relevant knowledge across handoffs while preventing unrelated
orders, roles and customers from leaking into recall.

**Implemented proof:** [typed memory](../src/delivery/typed_memory.py) stores
validated observations, server-derived provenance and append-only revisions.
Recall derives context from the current authenticated lease. Approved canonical
custody facts are exported in an assignment brief; another agent's private memory
is not shared. [Memory tests](../tests/test_typed_memory.py) cover source forgery,
current-order isolation, concurrent capacity, expiry and suppression of older
revisions. [Supply tests](../tests/test_supply_integration.py) restrict markets to
the current ingredient request; fleet tests isolate courier assignment attempts.

**Limit:** this is exact filtered recall and explicit fact sharing. Cross-order
learning, vector recall, automatic consolidation and managed Memory Bank are not
implemented. Typed observations cannot override operational truth. Expiry removes
recall eligibility while retaining operator audit history; it is not a deletion
policy. [Memory contracts](AGENT-MEMORY.md).

## 4. Cost and tool admission

**Goal:** bound work before execution and retain the cost of uncertain attempts.

**Implemented proof:** [runtime tests](../tests/test_agent_runtime.py) exercise
concurrent durable reservations and exhausted limits. Optional judge tests verify
six calls/50,688 reserved tokens per run, with 8,448 tokens reserved per dispatch
and no new call charge for a saved-result replay. [Cloud request tests](../tests/test_cloud_ai.py)
enforce a bounded numeric context; [gateway tests](../tests/test_gateway_policy.py)
deny invalid or infeasible requests before model invocation.
[Search tests](../tests/test_supply_search_service.py) retain admission reservations
after provider failures. Default local scenarios invoke no model.

**Limit:** `model_usd: 0` is a schema literal, not a working paid-GCP dollar ceiling.
Per-run limits, one Cloud Run instance and scale-to-zero do not cap project spend.
A durable gateway-wide currency admission ledger and comparative live cost per
successful task remain missing. Provider regressions use injected responses;
historical live verification is documented separately. [GCP components](GCP-COMPONENTS.md).

## 5. Evaluations

**Goal:** make expected behavior explicit and reproduce both safe outcomes and
failure cases.

**Implemented proof:** the [scenario manifest](../data/evals/agent-scenarios.json)
declares twelve scenarios and 49 typed criteria. The
[evaluator](../src/delivery/scenario_evals.py) runs real scoped workers in disposable
local test worlds; [receipt validation](../src/delivery/scenario_report.py)
recomputes results and checks source/configuration/repeat hashes. Missing criteria
receive no credit, a later pass cannot erase an earlier failure, and source drift
fails reproducibility. [Evaluator tests](../tests/test_scenario_evals.py) verify
these rules, local-only database guards and cleanup after fixture failure.

**Limit:** these are fixed rules-based development regressions. They do not measure
held-out LLM quality, memory-strategy superiority, architecture comparisons,
production latency or business uplift. Historical live GCP system cases also
include deterministic preflight denials; their pass count is not a model accuracy
score. [Evaluation methodology](AGENT-EVALS.md), [dated cloud evidence](GCP-VERIFICATION.md).

## 6. Observability and replay

**Goal:** explain what work executed, what it observed and why the recorded
business state changed.

**Implemented proof:** decisions retain tool receipts, recalled fact IDs/revisions,
memory writes and event lineage. The operator can inspect complete order history.
Supply replay reconstructs business projections and detects fact-hash corruption;
[delivery-fact tests](../tests/test_supply_delivery_facts.py) retain world and
dispatcher changes even after a household order becomes terminal.
[Health reporting](../src/delivery/health.py) distinguishes missing, partial,
failed, stale and source-outdated receipts. Its
[tests](../tests/test_health.py) prevent incomplete evidence from appearing green.
The optional gateway emits structured decision, version, usage and timing records.

**Limit:** business replay and recorded explanations do not expose private model
reasoning. Complete OpenTelemetry propagation, Cloud Trace, production dashboards,
alert policies and declared cloud log retention are not configured. Reading local
health does not query current GCP deployment status. Use [health semantics](HEALTH.md)
and the [GCP operations runbook](GCP-AI.md) for their distinct evidence boundaries.

# How this project's agents are built

Source review: 2026-10-28. This describes the executable implementation, not an
illustrative ADK design. Start with this document, then read the
[GCP component inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md) and
[enterprise architecture decisions](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md).

## The agent object

An agent is a frozen `LocalAgent` containing an authenticated `AgentScope`, a
validated `RoleSpec`, its scoped database identity and, for an explicitly enabled
GCP judge, a gateway origin. Its public work loop is `claim()` → `process(event)`.
The shared class is in [agent_runtime.py](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py).
`create_inventory_agent` is an alias of `create_agent`, not a separate framework.

Most agents use fixed Python decision policies. Restaurants can instead select
the [Google ADK adapter](ADK-RESTAURANT.md), with editable prompts/SOUL and granular
tools. Its current model is a scripted offline fixture; Gemini is not enabled.
Inventory arithmetic, sourcing,
consent, route selection and custody are enforced by domain code and SQL. The
recovery judge is the previously live-verified Google model path; restaurants now
also have a disabled-by-default, budgeted native Vertex adapter. The city is a realistic test
environment for those boundaries; running a city is not itself an LLM workload.

| Building block | Actual implementation | What it guarantees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Definition | Canonical `role.json` manifests, [JSON Schema](../config/agents/role.schema.json), `RoleSpec` and `RoleLimits` in [agent_specs.py](../src/delivery/agent_specs.py) | Strict fields, frozen objects, bounded limits and manifest-owned tool/topic subsets |
| Provisioning | `inventory_access`, `role_access`, `supply_access` in [agent_access.py](../src/delivery/agent_access.py) | Trusted controller creates a login, binds its scope and snapshots definition/hash |
| Factory | `create_agent` in [agent_runtime.py](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py) | Reads scope from authenticated SQL functions and checks the saved definition hash |
| Work delivery | `Queue` and [queue capability migration](../sql/migrations/014_queue_capability.sql) | Addressed claims, lease fencing, priorities, due time, retry/backoff and dead letters |
| Action boundary | `ScopedTools.invoke` and role-specific SQL functions | Fixed callable registry; authenticated scope and live budget/lease checks |
| Memory | [typed_memory.py](../src/delivery/typed_memory.py), [typed-memory migration](../sql/migrations/015_typed_memory.sql) | Typed observations, current-context recall, source events, expiry and revision history |
| Accountability | Decisions, tool receipts, memory read/write receipts and queued lineage | Inspect what the worker observed and changed, with business replay where implemented |

## From editable definition to an authenticated worker

1. The operator edits a supported role's `role.json` and `SOUL.md`, or a supply
   blueprint's agent/entity definitions. The canonical `role.json` is the only
   permission ceiling; blueprint and runtime profiles can narrow its grants.
   Editing a manifest cannot create a new tool implementation. SOUL text never
   grants permissions.
2. The loader validates the definition and resolves SOUL text. `RoleSpec.digest`
   hashes its canonical resolved JSON, including that text. Role-file SOUL paths
   are constrained to the supported definition directory.
3. The trusted controller creates a restricted PostgreSQL login per run/namespace.
   `agent_bindings` stores the login, run, namespace, agent ID, definition and hash;
   budget tables store the corresponding limits. Passwords stay in the controller's
   process and scoped connection objects, not in prompts or exported evidence.
4. `create_agent(dsn, agent_mode=..., cloud_endpoint=...)` calls `agent_scope()` and
   `agent_definition()` as that login. It rejects missing bindings, invalid hashes,
   incompatible judge modes and a cloud judge without an endpoint.
5. Later blueprint/role-file edits affect new runs. The running agent reads its
   frozen database definition. New supply runs additionally snapshot recipes,
   demand schedules and entity settings; blueprint updates use revision checking.
6. Normal run completion/failure retires the temporary logins through
   `retire_inventory_access`. Definitions and evidence can remain for inspection.
   Abrupt controller death still needs a durable supervisor/reaper.

For supply agents, [supply_models.py](../src/delivery/supply_models.py) defines
`AgentDefinition` and `EntityDefinition`; `supply_access` converts the frozen
run/entity settings into `RoleSpec`. They do not load restaurant/market role files
from `config/agents`. Display name, SOUL, simulated latency, search options and
bounded limits are editable. A fictional display name does not change a principal.

## What SOUL means today

SOUL is versioned and inspectable guidance. **The deterministic policies do not
interpret it.** Editing it does not teach a courier a new strategy or change stock
arithmetic. Business settings such as stock, hours, consent and latency have
explicit implemented effects.

The GCP judge does not receive its local role SOUL either. Its cloud container
has a separate fixed `systemInstruction` and `PROMPT_VERSION` in
[gateway.py](../infra/gcp-ai/gateway.py). Consequently, a local SOUL hash is not
proof of the exact model prompt. Cloud experiments must retain the gateway prompt
version/image digest as well as the local role definition hash.

The restaurant ADK adapter assembles platform instructions, the frozen role prompt
and SOUL, then supplies scoped tools and current-order recall. Its two offline
profiles demonstrate that instructions reach the actual ADK function-calling loop.
The scripted model implements those fixture strategies; this is not evidence of
generative-model quality. Permissions and budgets remain enforced independently.
Other roles and the cloud judge keep the behavior described above.

## Roles, namespaces and tools

`store` in internal binding tables is a namespace field; it is not always a shop.
Every role has typed `memory.read` and `memory.write`. The domain tools below are
prefixed exactly as their runtime registry names indicate.

| Role | Binding namespace | Domain tools | Typed fact kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inventory | `store-N` | `inventory.read/reserve/release/delay/receive` | `inventory.reservation`, `inventory.shipment` |
| Fulfillment | `fulfillment:store-N` | `fulfillment.read/pick` | `fulfillment.progress` |
| Dispatcher | `dispatcher:fleet` | `dispatch.read/assign/complete/recover/defer` | `delivery.progress` |
| Courier | `courier:<fleet-id>` | `courier.read/accept` | `courier.commitment` |
| Judge | `judge:fleet` | `judge.read/review` | `recovery.verdict` |
| Household | Entity ID | `supply.read/command` | `household.order` |
| Restaurant | Entity ID | `supply.read/command` | `restaurant.order` |
| Market | Entity ID | `supply.read/command` | `market.request` |

That table describes the default deterministic supply workers. An ADK restaurant
uses `restaurant.*` capabilities listed in the [ADK chapter](ADK-RESTAURANT.md)
and a separate restricted PostgreSQL group. It cannot call `supply.command` or
read the legacy broad supply context. Its typed memory contract remains unchanged.

Workflow roles use `queue.publish` within their topic/recipient policy. Supply
commands produce a fixed SQL outbox; the agent cannot choose arbitrary recipients.
Although `supply.search` is declared in the supply authority contract, it is not a
`ScopedTools.invoke` implementation. Restaurant/market search is the separate
authenticated `search_for_agent` path in
[supply_search_service.py](../src/delivery/supply_search_service.py); the fixed
`SupplyPolicy` does not automatically call it. Optional Jev search and its budgets
are separate from the GCP judge.

Examples of the actual queue contracts are inventory `basket.requested` →
`basket.reserved`, fulfillment → `basket.ready`, dispatcher → `courier.briefed`,
courier → `courier.accepted`, and failed delivery → judge `recovery.reviewed`.
Complete accepted/emitted sets live in each canonical `role.json`; the Madrid
service's queue topics are recorded in its `service_events` profile.
No role exposes a direct agent-call tool. Simulated phone calls are typed queued
messages, not telephony sessions or free-form LLM conversations.

## The existing HTTP communication endpoints

These local supply routes are implemented in
[supply_api.py](../src/delivery/supply_api.py). Their common prefix is
`/api/supply/runs/{run}/agents/{agent_id}`:

| Method / suffix | Authentication and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /channel` | Operator `X-Operator-Key`, matching configured `DELIVERY_OPERATOR_KEY`; issues a one-hour bearer channel for an active agent |
| `POST /claim` | Scoped bearer channel; claims an addressed queued event and returns its event/lease/attempt envelope |
| `POST /messages` | Scoped bearer plus matching envelope; processes the existing leased event, never arbitrary caller-supplied message content |
| `POST /calls` | Same mechanism, restricted to an owned household-intent lease |
| `POST /search` | Scoped bearer/envelope plus bounded query and frozen provider choice; restaurant/market search path |
| `POST /memory/recall` | Scoped bearer/envelope; consumes a tool allowance; only supported type/limit filters |
| `GET /memory` | Authenticated legacy route returns 410; broad memory retrieval is unavailable |

Envelope fields are `event_id`, `lease_token` and `attempt`. Database checks still
fence stale leases even after HTTP authentication. Blueprint, run/order history,
agent inspection and replay endpoints are separate **trusted operator views**;
they are not tools available to an agent.

Channel-token hashes, active agents and claimed HTTP lease references are currently
process-local dictionaries. They do not survive a restart or provide a shared
identity layer for several API replicas. Base Compose binds the app to loopback;
the Host/origin checks are local-demo safeguards, not enterprise authentication.
A cloud deployment needs workload OIDC/IAM and durable lease/controller handling;
publishing the existing operator API unchanged would expose broader inspection.

## One event, including the transaction boundaries

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Trusted controller
    participant A as Scoped LocalAgent
    participant Q as PostgreSQL queue
    participant T as Domain tools and memory
    C->>Q: Publish an addressed event
    A->>Q: Claim with role subscriptions
    Q-->>A: Event, attempt and fenced lease token
    A->>Q: Reserve attempt and full tool allowance
    Note over A,Q: Reservation commits before handling
    A->>Q: Begin effects transaction and validate lease
    A->>T: Read authoritative facts and current-context memory
    A->>T: Execute allowed actions and append memory revisions
    A->>Q: Record decision and publish outgoing events
    A->>Q: ACK in the same transaction
    Note over Q,T: Commit together, or roll back together
```

`LocalAgent.process` first commits the attempt/tool reservation. Optional GCP mode
then prepares a durable scoped request, commits its single-dispatch admission,
closes the worker's database connection, invokes the provider and saves its result
in a separate short transaction. Then `Queue.process` obtains the run
advisory lock and event row lock, checks the fence, reloads the authoritative
payload and invokes `handle`. The handler selects `InventoryPolicy`, `SupplyPolicy`
or `WorkflowPolicy`/`FleetPolicy` and records the decision before ACK commits.

Handler failure or lease expiry rolls back domain changes, memory, decision,
outgoing events and transactional tool charges. Failure scheduling happens
separately. Durable attempt/model reservations are not refunded. Deduplication
and domain invariants provide idempotent business effects; they do not establish
exactly-once external inference or billing. See [queue.py](../src/delivery/queue.py).

**Durable cloud path:** `FleetPolicy.cloud_judgement` only consumes a saved result;
it cannot invoke the provider. The effects transaction compares the saved context,
proposal, memory and simulated time with current authoritative observations before
SQL independently checks feasibility. A retry of the same source event reuses a
saved result without another model charge. An abandoned in-flight invocation has
an unknown outcome and fails closed rather than automatically resending. The
request snapshot and its preparatory read/tool receipts commit independently of
the final effects transaction. See [durable inference](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md),
[orchestration](../src/delivery/durable_inference.py) and the
[request state machine](../sql/migrations/016_durable_inference.sql).

## Permissions and memory are enforced outside the prompt

Logins are non-superuser, cannot create databases/roles, replicate or bypass RLS.
Scope derives from PostgreSQL `session_user`, not a model-supplied store ID or
mutable connection setting. Inventory can inspect its own run/store stock through
RLS. Other domain roles receive narrow functions/projections rather than raw stock
tables. Tools require a live lease, supported event and durable budget ticket.

Typed memory writes derive owner, order/shipment, subject, source event, revision
and observation time on the server. Bodies are limited to 2 KiB; TTL is 1–86,400
simulated seconds, additionally constrained by the role's live entry/byte caps.
Recall defaults to eight facts, permits at most sixteen and bounds complete result
envelopes to 8 KiB. Market recall is ingredient-request-specific; courier recall
also matches the assignment attempt. A newer expired revision suppresses older
values. Raw current/history/legacy memory tables are denied to agents.

Expiry controls recall eligibility; it does **not** erase audit history. Revisions
and decision inspection remain until trusted cleanup. There is no pgvector search,
cross-order learning, automatic summary consolidation or managed Memory Bank.
[Memory contracts and retention](AGENT-MEMORY.md) contain the detailed semantics.

The controller, operator UI/API, host and fixed Python policies are trusted. One
Python process can hold several scoped connections; this is not a container/OS
sandbox for hostile Python. M1 also retains its older shared-account runtime.
Enterprise workload identities and process boundaries must complement these
database controls; adding an ADK subagent object alone provides neither.

## Budgets and reproducible evidence

The original inventory profile has 100 attempt reservations, eight tool slots per
attempt, 400 per run, 32 live facts and 16,384 live body bytes. These are not global
defaults for every business role. Supply sessions set aggregate allowances of
12,000 attempts/48,000 tool slots and resolve larger dispatcher/courier profiles
before freezing them. Inspect the saved definition and budget for a particular run.

The optional [judge-gcp definition](../config/agents/judge-gcp/role.json) permits six
model calls and 50,688 reserved tokens. Each request reserves 8,448 tokens
(8,192 input + 256 output). `model_usd: 0` is a schema literal, **not a working
dollar ceiling** for paid GCP mode. Gateway-wide monetary admission remains a gap.

```bash
make health
make eval-agents
```

The [role battery](AGENT-EVALS.md) runs actual scoped agents on twelve fixed
scenarios and scores 49 declared criteria. The 2026-10-28 receipt records 392
passing tests and matching repeated seed-731 outcomes. This is development
regression/isolation evidence, not proof of LLM quality, scalability or production
readiness. [GCP live verification](GCP-VERIFICATION.md) is a separate dated record.
