pages.body:
# Google ADK restaurant agent

This slice uses **Google ADK 2.13.0** and its real `LlmAgent`, `Runner`, function
tools, model callbacks and session service. The default model is explicitly a
scripted offline `BaseLlm` double. A native Vertex/Gemini adapter is implemented
behind an explicit deployment gate and monetary budget; it is disabled by default
and was exercised explicitly with both SOULs on Vertex on 2026-10-29. There is no automatic
paid-provider fallback. Offline results demonstrate integration
and enforcement; they do not measure a language model's understanding of SOUL.

## Reusable building blocks

Source map: [template contract](../src/delivery/adk_contracts.py),
[ADK turn and tools](../src/delivery/adk_restaurant.py),
[native model adapter](../src/delivery/adk_models.py),
[offline model double](../src/delivery/adk_offline.py),
[scoped turn/transaction SQL](../sql/migrations/017_adk_restaurant.sql),
[Vertex admission SQL](../sql/migrations/018_adk_vertex_admission.sql), and
[executable checks](../tests/test_adk_restaurant.py).
The editable [role prompt](../config/agents/restaurant-adk/PROMPT.md),
[speed SOUL](../config/agents/restaurant-adk/SOUL-speed.md) and
[cost SOUL](../config/agents/restaurant-adk/SOUL-cost.md) are resolved into the
frozen restaurant definition.

`RestaurantBrain` is the validated template contract. A restaurant instance
combines that contract with its existing entity, authenticated database identity,
role limits, role prompt and SOUL. The operator can edit the prompt/SOUL and bounded
budgets in `/restaurant-lab`, through its revision-checked blueprint endpoint, or
in advanced agent JSON. Choose **Override for this entity** or **Edit shared role
template**, then **Google ADK · offline model fixture**. The two Load profile
prompts options initialize Elena (shortest quoted lead time) and Mateo (lowest
quoted procurement fee). Saving a blueprint affects new runs, never an existing
agent's frozen definition.

`config/agents/restaurant-adk/PROMPT.md` supplies the reusable role prompt;
`SOUL-speed.md` and `SOUL-cost.md` supply the initial profiles. The template endpoint
`GET /api/supply/agent-templates` exposes resolved, approved local templates. No
configuration field names an executable module, arbitrary URL or credential.
Tool references can remove supported capabilities; extending authority requires
reviewed code, permissions and tests. A template cannot grant another role's tools.

Effective instructions combine a fixed platform boundary, the editable role prompt
and editable SOUL. A callable instruction provider preserves literal braces in
operator text. ADK initially receives only the leased event identifier; the actual
order and event facts come from scoped SQL tools. Forged caller-side event bodies
cannot enter model context or select a different order. Every turn gets a fresh, private
in-memory ADK session. Cross-event working memory comes from the existing typed
Postgres recall functions; broad session history is not shared between agents.

## Granular tools

| ADK function | Capability | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read_order` | `restaurant.order` | Current order, event, deadline and canonical alternative |
| `read_pantry` | `restaurant.pantry` | This kitchen's physical stock and reservations |
| `read_recipe` | `restaurant.recipe` | This meal's frozen recipe and units |
| `find_suppliers` | `restaurant.suppliers` | Open markets' public fees and estimated lead times; no private stock |
| `recall_order_memory` | `memory.read` | Current-order, restaurant-owned, unexpired typed observations |
| `search_ingredients` | `supply.search` (optional) | Scoped ingredient relevance; separate local/Jev provider and budget |
| `request_missing_ingredients` | `restaurant.request_supply` | Stage a supplier choice; SQL calculates shortages and queues requests |
| `confirm_order` | `restaurant.confirm` | Stage pantry-only acceptance; a shortage invalidates the proposal |
| `receive_ingredient` | `restaurant.receive` | Stage receipt of the ingredient addressed by this event |
| `prepare_meal` | `restaurant.cook` | Stage cooking after arrival, consent and timing checks |
| `offer_substitution` | `restaurant.offer` | Stage the safe alternative; queue the household's approval request |
| `decline_order` | `restaurant.decline` | Stage a bounded reason and reservation release |
| `finish_decision` | `restaurant.finish` | Seal one staged action with a brief explanation |

The model chooses which tools to use and which supplier/action to propose. The
shared runtime does not choose the sourcing strategy. The offline model double
implements the two documented fixture strategies to exercise that interface;
it should be replaced with an evaluated generative model for intelligence tests.

Quotes are synthetic entity settings. `procurement_fee_cents` is editable entity
data. Lead time is an estimate derived from grid distance and supplier delay,
not a guaranteed route ETA or stock promise. Supermarket workers continue using
their deterministic policy and reply only through queued messages.

## Transaction and recovery boundaries

1. Claim the addressed event and commit its ordinary tool/event budget ticket.
2. Begin a durable restaurant turn containing the frozen definition hash, canonical
   event payload and scoped business snapshot. A nonce fences the original owner.
3. Before **each** ADK model call, save a request hash and conservative token
   reservation. Close the SQL connection before model execution. Save the model
   completion receipt separately. No provider/model retries are automatic.
4. Read tools each use a short authenticated transaction and retain a receipt.
   Write tools only stage a proposal; they make no stock changes or agent calls.
5. Save the completed plan durably. The final effects transaction rechecks the
   current business snapshot, recalled memory versions/expiry, event/action pair,
   permitted tool receipts and live lease. SQL computes physical quantities and
   enforces supplier validity, exclusions, consent, reservations and cooking.
6. Commit domain effects, queue outbox, replay facts, typed outcome memory,
   decision receipt, applied marker and event ACK together.

A saved completed plan can be consumed after lease reclamation without repeating
ADK calls. Death during an unfinished turn marks it unknown on reclamation and
fails closed; it does not regenerate a partially completed decision. Changed
business observations or expired/revised recalled facts invalidate a saved plan.
Such turns need explicit operator handling. This chooses bounded retries and
auditability over automatic availability; external exactly-once billing is not claimed.

## Authorization and budgets

ADK restaurants use their own `lab_restaurant_adk_executor` PostgreSQL group, not
the legacy supply executor. It has no stock, memory-history, turn-table or broad
`supply_context`/`supply_command` grants. All granular functions reconstruct scope
from `session_user`, a live addressed lease and a durable budget ticket. The model
cannot supply a run, order, namespace or agent identity in tool arguments. ADK's
tool callback also rejects unknown fields/types before execution.

The existing event/tool/memory limits remain independent of instructions. New
brain limits cap model calls per event and per restaurant/run, serialized token
reservations, request bytes, output tokens and wall time. A run-wide ceiling also
limits aggregate restaurant calls/tokens. Reservations survive failures and are
not refunded. Bytes of the serialized text-only request conservatively reserve
input tokens; configured output allowance is reserved too. This is not a tokenizer
or a measurement of actual Gemini usage. Offline inference has zero provider
cost. Native Vertex admission additionally reserves money at the frozen approved
input/output rates, rounds upward and checks the restaurant's `usd_limit` plus a
$10 run-wide reservation ceiling. The unpriced admission helper is private.
Reservations survive timeouts and crashes, with no automatic refund. These limits
bound admitted work at configured rates; they do not enforce a billing-account
cap or compensate for a provider tariff change. Unknown actual billing stays unknown.
ADK model limits live in `brain`; the legacy `RoleLimits` model fields retain the
older judge contract. Operator inspection shows the separate ADK reservation
counters rather than treating those legacy zero fields as actual ADK usage.

The trusted local host/controller remains outside this isolation boundary. This
is not an OS sandbox for arbitrary agent code. Inspection endpoints are trusted
operator views and are not registered ADK tools.

## Optional native Vertex model adapter

`adk_models.py` constructs ADK's `Gemini` with Vertex enabled, a specific approved
project/region/model, stable API version `v1`, ADC credentials and one HTTP attempt.
It never accepts an API key or arbitrary model endpoint from a prompt/blueprint.
A Vertex brain requires a positive `usd_limit` and a `vertex` profile containing
`project`, `location`, `model`, `input_usd_per_million` and `output_usd_per_million`.
The trusted deployment must separately set `DELIVERY_ADK_VERTEX_ENABLED=1` and
`DELIVERY_ADK_VERTEX_PROFILE` to that exact approved JSON profile. Missing approval,
different project/model/pricing, unapproved adapters or exhausted budgets fail closed.
The normal UI loads only offline profiles; configuring Vertex requires an operator
to prepare the advanced definition and deployment policy explicitly.

No credentials are discovered until an approved native model is actually invoked.
The local Compose defaults contain no ADC mount. In a GCP workload, ADC should
come from its least-privilege runtime identity. Test profile prices and project IDs
are fictional inputs, not recommended Google prices. Model availability, region,
current tariffs and IAM are operator deployment choices. The explicit live comparison
below exercises this adapter without enabling paid execution in the normal city UI.

## Verification and GCP direction

Run the reproducible offline checks with the local Postgres services available:

```bash
make test-adk
```

`make demo-adk` retains two one-order runs for inspecting the profiles in the UI
and writes `artifacts/adk-restaurants-demo.json`. It changes no saved blueprint,
uses only this project's local database, and never selects Vertex. Default city
demand is much larger than this bounded comparison; model/tool budgets still
stop an over-budget ADK worker rather than silently enabling an unbounded run.

Tests use only `delivery_test`, restricted identities, real ADK function calls and
an HTTP-blocking fixture. They cover both profiles through sourcing and physical
delivery, replay, prompts reaching ADK, foreign roles/runs, raw-table/legacy denial,
budgets, stale stock, invalid suppliers, unfinished-turn rejection and saved-plan
recovery. A worker is also terminated as a real process after saving its plan.
The health dashboard lists these cases under **ADK restaurant agents**.

Google-native components implemented here are ADK, Google Gen AI types and a gated
keyless Vertex model adapter. The
existing isolated Terraform Cloud Run/Vertex recovery judge is separate. The
local city and Postgres remain free local infrastructure. Production work still
includes billing reconciliation, broader model-quality evaluation and a supervised worker.
Cloud Run or managed-runtime hosting must be Terraform-owned before deployment;
ADK names or sessions do not create IAM identities. No new GCP resource is required
or provisioned by the offline checks.

## Historical Vertex and Jev comparison

The native restaurant worker stays local and impersonates a dedicated, keyless
`restaurant-adk` service account in the isolated simulation project. Terraform
owns the identity, its `aiplatform.endpoints.predict` grant and the permitted
operator impersonation binding. This mode enables the project's billing link
without creating Cloud Run, Artifact Registry, Cloud SQL or a managed agent runtime.
The existing judge gateway is not deployed for these tests. Project, APIs and IAM
remain when billing is parked.

```bash
make gcp-vertex-start
make demo-adk-vertex
make gcp-stop
make gcp-status
```

Each SOUL gets one synthetic pizza order, an empty pantry and three public
supplier quotes. Elena should prioritize lead time; Mateo should prioritize
procurement fee. Both use the same ADK tool implementation. Gemini decides the
tool sequence and supplier from the prompt and SOUL; the SQL layer validates
authority, quantities, consent and event effects. No paid model selects the stock
quantities or bypasses the queue.

The reviewed model is `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, global, standard text PayGo:
$0.30 / million input tokens, $2.50 / million output tokens including thinking,
and $0.03 / million cached input tokens, checked 2026-10-29. Gemini 3 uses minimal
thinking for this bounded trial. Global is deliberate for synthetic data and
does not assert EU processing residency. The retired 2.5 model is not used.

Jev `jev-1.14.0` is an optional `supply.search` capability, not a general planner.
The model may call `search_ingredients` with a canonical ingredient ID from the
current recipe. The server selects the already scoped restaurant index and
frozen review provider. Jev receives ingredient labels, units and a relevance
question; it receives no inventory counts, household conversations or typed memory.
Its result is an observation. Availability is read again locally; reservation
and supplier communication still require the transactional tools and event queue.
Its input-only tariff is $0.042 / million tokens, output free. An API key is held
in ignored `.env.jev` and passed only to the one-shot worker.

The comparison admits at most $0.20 Vertex work per SOUL ($0.40 together),
60 calls per agent, eight per event, 1,024 output tokens per call, and a 30-second
event deadline. Each agent also gets three Jev calls and 24,000 reserved input
tokens: together $0.002016 maximum at the reviewed Jev tariff. No automatic
provider retries, provider fallback or fresh paid experiments follow a failure.
An exclusive execution lock prevents concurrent launches. Explicit receipt recovery
can re-read finished runs without repeating calls; reviewed follow-up experiments
account for previous known costs, reserving the full allowance for unknown calls,
against a cumulative $0.50 Vertex limit. Operator-controlled local files and
SQL admission are not a billing-account spending cap.

The retained live comparison delivered both meals, with 25 Gemini calls and three
Jev calls per SOUL. Elena selected `market-a` (90-second quoted lead time); Mateo
selected `market-b` (50-cent fee). Both runs acknowledged 24 events, had zero
retries/dead letters, conserved stock and replayed correctly. Median Gemini call
latency was 800 ms for Elena and 769 ms for Mateo. Their Vertex costs calculated
from actual usage were $0.01214980 and $0.01269700; Jev was $0.000136962 each.
Including the initial trial, total usage-derived cost was $0.039755624. Billing
was then disabled, retaining 15 foundation resources. A live impersonated IAM
probe received HTTP 403 / PERMISSION_DENIED for `resourcemanager.projects.get`.

These two synthetic orders prove integration and the intended SOUL distinction;
they are not a general model-quality benchmark or proof of cost/latency savings
from a Jev cascade. That baseline invokes Gemini on routine arrival and cooking
events. The Jev-first implementation below compares that baseline with selective
escalation on the same scenarios.
One recovered receipt has no whole-run wall time; per-call latency and token
metadata were durably retained and remain available.

[AI evidence](/agent-traces) shows the retained comparison, system prompts and
SOULs, tool declarations, model-visible messages, function calls, tool results,
selected memory with provenance/expiry/version, provider model version, latency,
tokens and usage-derived costs. Full private rows are not granted to agents.
The page never starts inference. Costs calculated from actual token metadata are
separate from invoice totals, credits, tax and project-wide charges; missing
metadata remains unknown. Previous attempts remain in the local JSON receipt.

Source links: [operator evidence reader](../src/delivery/adk_evidence.py),
[paid comparison](../scripts/demo_adk_vertex.py),
[temporary impersonated ADC launcher](../scripts/run_adk_vertex.py),
[model trace schema](../sql/migrations/019_adk_model_traces.sql),
[scoped search grants](../sql/migrations/020_adk_scoped_search.sql),
[canonical business snapshots](../sql/migrations/021_canonical_supply_context.sql),
and [usage-cost and operator-boundary tests](../tests/test_adk_evidence.py).

An initial real run exposed unordered JSON inventory arrays: equal stock facts
could fail stale-state validation after a different query plan. Canonical ordering
fixes that comparison while preserving version/quantity checks. A regression test
rewrites physical stock rows without changing their business values; existing
stale-stock tests continue to reject actual changes.

## Jev-first decisions and bounded model selection

Set `brain.routing.strategy` to `jev_first` in an ADK restaurant definition. The
operator editor exposes the routing strategy, confidence and margin; advanced JSON
also controls the pinned Jev model, router instructions, calls, tokens and money.
Leaving routing unset preserves the existing ADK model tool loop. These settings
are frozen with the agent at run creation; editing a template cannot change a live run.

The execution path is:

1. Physical ingredient-arrival and cooking events follow their single validated
   protocol action without a model. This does not choose suppliers or substitutions.
2. For an order, approval or shortage judgment, the worker retrieves only this
   restaurant's current recipe, required pantry rows, public supplier quotes and
   selected current-order memory. Household identity, raw call transcript, other
   orders and supermarket stock are omitted from Jev's request.
3. One Jev request classifies requested work (finite action/factual receipt versus
   explicit reasoning), the permitted action, and, when sourcing is needed, a
   quoted supplier versus abstention. A stocked-pantry call omits both the supplier
   lookup and its irrelevant question. The editable role prompt and SOUL remain
   inputs. Jev cannot invent tool names, models or URLs.
4. Direct action requires confidence at least **0.85**, top-to-second probability
   margin at least **0.20** on every relevant question, valid response shape and
   locally supported evidence. Stock sufficiency, replacement consent and tool
   authority remain mandatory. These thresholds are configurable starting values,
   not a calibrated guarantee of correctness on this domain.
5. Jev's request for reasoning, low certainty, unsupported action or an invalid/
   missing provider response permits the separately budgeted Gemini tool loop.
   An exhausted router budget or missing deployment permission fails closed.
6. Both paths stage the same typed plan through the same granular tools. SQL
   validates and commits effects, memory, outbox and ACK atomically. Jev never
   contacts a supermarket directly or changes stock.

The approved executor registry currently contains **no further model** and the
frozen Gemini Vertex profile. Jev chooses whether that model is needed; it does
not gain permission to choose a more expensive model, provider, region or identity.
Adding another approved tier requires a reviewed adapter, deployment allowlist,
tariff and eval cases. This keeps model selection editable within an explicit
security and cost boundary.

Before dispatch, Postgres stores the Jev request and reserves input bytes plus
2,048 tokens at the pinned input tariff. A single durable router receipt is allowed
per event. The result, probabilities, confidence, margin, executor, reason, known
usage and latency are saved before downstream Gemini admission or effects. Network
calls run outside transactions. Unknown usage keeps the full reservation. No
provider retry or automatic resumption repeats a pending request after a crash.
The ordinary saved-plan recovery path remains available after a complete result.

This is currently a **restaurant** decision adapter. Other roles share selectable
memory and enforcement but retain their existing deterministic or judge policy;
they are not silently converted to autonomous Jev agents.

Run the bounded matched comparison explicitly:

```bash
make gcp-vertex-start
make demo-adk-routing
make gcp-stop
make gcp-status
```

It executes one order each for speed, cost and an explicitly requested fast-versus-
cheap explanation, in baseline and cascade mode: six runs. Each pair uses the same
SOUL, city seed, demand and typed memory. Baseline retains the prior initial Jev
mozzarella relevance search; cascade uses Jev for decisions and optional relevance
search only after Gemini escalation. This compares the two complete configurations,
not an isolated causal effect of one provider. The combined admission allowance is
$0.54 Vertex plus less than $0.01 Jev, within $0.60. The permanent experiment marker
prevents repeat spending, even if its UI receipt is lost. The normal UI has no keys,
ADC mount or paid deployment gate.

[AI evidence](/agent-traces) exposes each arm's outcomes, provider counts, costs,
wall time and routing decisions. A cost saving is reported only for a pair with
matched supplier choice, delivery, queue, replay, stock and complete known usage.
Provider medians have different call mixes; baseline legacy Jev search latency is
an aggregate operation and is excluded from provider p50. One order per arm is a
smoke comparison, not a statistically established quality or speed improvement.

### Live routing result: 2026-10-29

The complete six-arm comparison **failed its outcome gate**, with four meals
delivered. The failure remains visible in `/agent-traces`; this is not a release
approval for making the cascade the default.

| SOUL | Baseline Gemini calls / cost / wall time | Jev-first Gemini calls / cost / wall time | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Speed | 23 / 0.011208962 USD / 37.634 s | 7 / 0.002920592 USD / 11.845 s | Both delivered; same supplier, conserved stock and matching replay |
| Cost | 25 / 0.012906462 USD / 32.460 s | 6 / 0.002402218 USD / 10.369 s | Cascade rejected an invented `finish_finish_decision` tool; no applied sourcing effects |
| Explain trade-off | 23 / 0.012891262 USD / 31.913 s | 6 / 0.002820798 USD / 12.448 s | Jev explicitly chose Gemini; its 574-character finish summary exceeded the 500-character contract |

Costs include actual reported Vertex and Jev usage at the frozen tariffs. The
failed runs' lower costs do not support a savings claim. Only the speed pair
matched outcomes: its observed cost fell by 73.9% and wall time by 68.5%. These
changes combine five no-model protocol events, Jev routing and less relevance
searching; they cannot be attributed to Jev alone.

All three live judgments escalated: speed confidence was 0.68, cost 0.56, and
reasoning 0.84 with an explicit Gemini choice. The 0.85 direct-action threshold
was not lowered after observing results. Direct Jev actions were verified with
injected responses locally, **not established by these live trials**. Jev router
latency was 208, 162 and 157 ms respectively. The provider-mix median in the
operator table includes downstream Gemini calls and is a different measurement.

After the cost failure, the original attempt stopped. A reviewed, one-time
continuation dispatched only the two untouched reasoning plans, under the same
six original configurations and cumulative ceilings. It did not retry a failed
event, replace a run, reset a budget or overwrite earlier evidence. Hashes of the
four preserved arms were checked before and after continuation. The second failure
stopped that continuation; all six planned arms had then been attempted.

Total known usage was **0.045150294 USD**, with **0.460544866 USD** conservatively
accounted using reservations for admitted work, below the 0.60 USD ceiling. No
usage was unknown. Invoice reconciliation remains pending. The retained summary
is `docs/evidence/jev-routing-comparison.json`; full local model/tool receipts
remain in `artifacts/adk-route-comparison.json`.

The next quality gate is stronger model-visible tool constraints and bounded
handling of malformed proposals, followed by a new, explicitly budgeted evaluation.
Scope, consent, stock validation and summary limits must remain enforced. The
existing failed examples must remain in the evaluation set; repeatedly rerunning
until a green sample appears would conceal the failure rate.

Sources: [Jev decision adapter](../src/delivery/jev_routing.py),
[router admission and result schema](../sql/migrations/022_jev_decision_routing.sql),
[local failure/isolation checks](../tests/test_jev_routing.py),
[matched comparison runner](../scripts/compare_agent_routing.py).

## Tool-contract enforcement and correction

Gemini requests now use `VALIDATED` function calling with an explicit allowlist
derived from this frozen agent's actual tools. The platform instructions, role
prompt and `finish_decision` declaration state the 1–500-character summary limit.
Google's function schema support does not make arbitrary string-length constraints
a server guarantee; Python and SQL continue to enforce the bound independently.

A completed model proposal can receive a structured `tool_contract` response for
an invented function name or an invalid summary length. An invented name is never
aliased or executed. A long summary is never silently truncated. The agent must
propose an exact declared function or rewrite its explanation while keeping its
original staged action. Successful `finish_decision` ends the ADK loop, avoiding
a further model call just to summarize the saved decision.

Postgres records each rejection in the existing private tool-receipt ledger,
under the current authenticated turn, nonce and lease. At most two corrections
are allowed per event, serialized with the live turn lock. Each costs an ordinary
tool slot, and each subsequent model call needs its own durable token/money
admission. The correction helper requires a completed model response and refuses
unfinished dispatches, finished plans and foreign roles. Scope-bearing arguments,
disabled tools, budget denials, stale facts and lease failures remain fatal. No
provider timeout or unknown dispatch is retried by this mechanism.

Local tests replay both observed failures, verify one staging receipt and one
valid finish before atomic effects, and terminate repeated malformed proposals
without sourcing. Cross-role helper calls and scope injection remain denied.

The one-shot live verification is separate from the original failed comparison:

```bash
make gcp-vertex-start
make verify-adk-contracts
make gcp-stop
```

It runs three one-order cases: a stocked pantry for direct Jev confirmation,
Mateo's cost explanation and Elena's speed-versus-fee explanation. The latter
cases explicitly request reasoned explanations to exercise Gemini's tool contract.
They are repair checks, not a new paired architecture benchmark. Thresholds remain
0.85 confidence and 0.20 margin. Each case admits one Jev call and no legacy
relevance searches; Vertex admission is at most 0.06 USD in each Gemini case.
The combined conservative reservation ceiling is 0.1215 USD, within a 0.15 USD
allowance. A permanent marker prevents automatic repeat spending.

The direct case uses an offline secondary-model profile with a one-token
admission ceiling. If Jev is uncertain, it cannot dispatch any secondary model.
Success requires an actual validated Jev `direct` / `confirm` response, physical
delivery, and an empty model-call ledger—not merely zero Gemini cost. All cases
must preserve stock, replay and queue invariants and deny raw stock/model/router
table access through the restaurant's actual login. The normal UI retains no
provider credentials or paid opt-in. `/agent-traces` shows the new results above
the unchanged failed comparison.

Sources: [correction admission and receipt function](../sql/migrations/025_adk_contract_corrections.sql),
[bounded live verifier](../scripts/verify_adk_contracts.py).
Official references: [Google function-calling modes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/tools/function-calling),
[ADK tool callback responses](https://adk.dev/callbacks/types-of-callbacks/).

### Repair verification: 2026-10-29

All three new cases passed with real Jev and Vertex. The earlier failed six-arm
comparison remains unchanged and visible below this verification in the UI.

| Case | Jev / Gemini calls | Known token cost | Router latency / run wall time | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Iris, stocked pantry | 1 / 0 | 0.000048216 USD | 172 ms / 4.783 s | Jev selected direct confirmation; one delivered meal |
| Mateo, procurement tradeoff | 1 / 6 | 0.002603334 USD | 154 ms / 12.123 s | Gemini chose market-b and saved a valid short explanation |
| Elena, speed tradeoff | 1 / 6 | 0.002854914 USD | 174 ms / 12.490 s | Gemini chose market-a and saved a valid short explanation |

The exact router latencies and per-call measurements are retained in
`docs/evidence/adk-contract-verification.json`; the UI's provider-mix median is a
different measurement. Iris's real response selected both `direct` and `confirm`
with probability/confidence 1.0. Her run contains no offline or Vertex model
dispatches, no supplier lookup and no supplier selection question. The one-token
secondary-model fence remained in place. SQL enforced physical pantry sufficiency,
and the confirm/cook flow completed through twelve queue events.

Both Gemini cases used `VALIDATED` declared functions and produced legal finish
summaries without needing a correction. Offline ADK regression tests separately
replayed the actual invented-name and 574-character failures and verified bounded
correction, unchanged staged effects, exhausted correction denial and role/lease
isolation. Every live case denied raw stock, model-ledger and router-ledger reads
through its active restaurant login and passed stock, queue and replay checks.

Two earlier Jev-only probes stopped at confidence 0.82 and 0.72, with no secondary
model dispatch. They exposed a broad self-assessment question and unrelated
supplier context. The final revision classifies the requested kind of work and
retrieves supplier context only when relevant. It keeps the 0.85 confidence and
0.20 margin gates. Each follow-up required review, a new configuration/run and a
permanent marker; prior raw receipts and conservative reservations carry forward.
No failed request was resent or overwritten.

Across all three attempts, known token cost was **0.005610540 USD** and conservative
accounting was **0.06073198 USD**, below the shared **0.15 USD** cap. Final-attempt
usage alone was 0.005506464 USD. These are frozen-tariff calculations, with invoice
reconciliation pending. Billing was disabled afterward through the guarded
Terraform plan; the project and fifteen free foundation resources remain, with
no Cloud Run service or billable runtime in state. The local evidence preview has
no Jev key, ADC mount or paid Vertex gate.

This is a three-order repair smoke check. It establishes a real direct Jev
decision for this stocked-pantry case; it does not establish held-out quality,
production calibration, broad savings or automatic recovery of uncertain calls.

Official deployment references: [Gemini model lifecycle](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/model-versions),
[3.5 Flash-Lite capabilities](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/3-5-flash-lite),
[Vertex pricing](https://cloud.google.com/model-garden/pricing),
[Jev models and pricing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models), and
[Jev typed questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives).

References: [ADK instructions and tools](https://adk.dev/agents/llm-agents/),
[identity and tool enforcement](https://adk.dev/safety/),
[runtime limits](https://adk.dev/runtime/runconfig/), and
[ADK on Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/single-agent-ai-system-adk-cloud-run).

# Agent memory: records, recall and storage

The durable memory boundary is implemented in Python/Postgres. The optional
[restaurant ADK adapter](ADK-RESTAURANT.md) uses this typed recall through a scoped
function tool; its ADK session is fresh per event and contains no other order's
conversation. Its default model is an offline fixture; explicit paid experiments
use native Gemini on Vertex and optional Jev routing. We do not run LangGraph,
OpenAI Agents SDK or a managed Memory Bank. The references below guide the design;
we have not benchmarked this project as state of the art.
The default city remains local, with model providers disabled.

## What exists today

| Layer | Current implementation | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operational truth | Transactional stock, reservations, orders and delivery custody in Postgres | A memory entry cannot change stock or override feasibility checks |
| Agent recall | Typed, versioned observations for the authenticated role and current incoming order | Lease-bound database functions; latest unexpired matching facts only |
| Audit | Queue lineage, decisions and replay facts; successful memory writes commit with the decision and ACK | Operator inspection is broader than agent recall; it is not an agent tool |
| Memory changes | Append-only revisions retain owner, order, source event, observation time, expiry and previous revision | Operator reconstructs diffs; write receipts never expose previous bodies |
| Conversation | Named fictional participants and readable queue messages, with memory changes at the receiving step | Presentation only; no invented LLM dialogue or changes to security principals |

The old `last:<order>` JSON entries remain operator history; agents cannot read or
write that legacy table. They are not automatically promoted to typed facts.
Order history can inspect archived writes after live recall expires.
Older records without a captured baseline show **previous value unavailable**;
expiry is distinguished from an active previous value. Scheduled delivery time
is labeled **Due** when the actual enqueue simulation time cannot be established.

## Typed memory and selective recall

Nine version-one contracts cover inventory reservations and shipment observations,
fulfillment progress, dispatcher progress, courier commitments, recovery verdicts,
household orders, restaurant orders and supermarket requests. Bodies reject
unknown fields and invalid values in both Python and Postgres. The SQL catalogue
retains each schema; a regression test checks that Python and SQL agree.

`memory.write(kind=..., body=..., ttl_seconds=3600)` records an observation of a
scoped tool outcome. The server supplies the owner, run, context, subject, source
event, observation time, revision and expiry. Callers cannot supply these fields.
Repeated writes for the same source/type/subject are idempotent; different content
or TTL under that source is rejected. Per-agent live count/body-byte caps are
serialized across concurrent writes. History persists until trusted operator
cleanup of the run/source events; expiry removes eligibility for recall, not audit.
The local supplier policy keeps pending reservations for one simulated hour and
finished/forwarded requests for one minute. Those short-lived terminal revisions
still suppress the older reservation and remain in history. This prevents closed
ingredient requests from occupying the default live-memory budget for an hour;
the capacity limit itself is unchanged.

`memory.read(kinds=None, limit=8)` has no order or namespace parameter. SQL derives
them from the authenticated session and current leased event. Supermarkets recall
only the current ingredient request; couriers only the addressed assignment
attempt. Results include source events, observation/expiry times and revision IDs,
with a maximum of 16 facts and 8 KiB for the full result envelopes. These canonical reads use exact indexed filters. An explicit semantic profile
adds ranking after this authorization step and rechecks SQL before returning facts. A newer expired revision suppresses
older revisions even if their original TTL has not elapsed. Repeatable-read and
serializable transactions are rejected so old snapshots cannot revive history.

Agent HTTP callers use `POST .../agents/{agent}/memory/recall` with their bearer
token and current event ID, lease token and attempt. Only type/limit filters are
accepted. The previous broad `GET .../memory` returns 410. HTTP recall consumes a
reserved tool slot, as does a direct SQL call. Decisions record which fact IDs and
versions were recalled; the operator can inspect this in an order's memory section.

Agents have no table access to current or historical memories or decision bodies.
Queue claim/ACK/failure/publication and tool charges use fixed database functions;
raw lease extension, event forgery, budget-counter resets and history browsing are
denied. These restrictions also cover existing role logins after migration.

Facts remain observations: stock, consent, routing and custody are authoritative in
the domain database. The fixed worker commits memory, decision, outbox and ACK in
one transaction. This atomic worker behavior is tested; SQL source authenticity
does not certify that an arbitrary authorized client's observation is true or
force a client to combine separate SQL statements into one transaction. The host,
operator API and fixed Python code remain trusted; agents have no arbitrary SQL,
network or code tool. This is not an OS sandbox for hostile code.

## Selectable per-agent memory

Each shared role template or individual entity can select a memory profile in
`/restaurant-lab`. Entity overrides are frozen at run creation. Leaving the profile
unset preserves legacy recall. A profile changes the context an agent receives,
with these bounded choices:

| Mode | Context returned to an ADK restaurant or Jev router | Useful when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | No prior facts | The current event and authoritative tools are sufficient |
| `text` | Concise factual lines with source, version and expiry references | A few observations fit naturally in a short prompt |
| `json` | Compact structured facts with a scope envelope and provenance | A small machine-readable record is sufficient |
| `typed` | Canonical typed fact envelopes | Decisions need explicit revisions, relationships and expiry |
| `semantic` | Authorized facts ranked by meaning, returned as typed envelopes | Relevant prior observations need ranking within the same order |

All modes keep canonical typed writes and revision history for audit. `none`
disables recall, not evidence retention. Text and JSON are projections of scoped
facts, not an unrestricted scratchpad or a second source of truth. The model
cannot pick a foreign namespace, write arbitrary JSON, fetch the whole chat or
turn a memory statement into inventory authority. Selecting a mode does not provision infrastructure. Semantic mode needs the
packaged local embedding model and pgvector, or explicitly configured Vertex
Vector Search. No summarizer or managed Memory Bank is used.

Profiles cap the number of facts (1–8), complete UTF-8 representation bytes
(256–8,192), and maximum fact lifetime (60–86,400 simulated seconds). Defaults are
eight facts, 8 KiB and one hour. SQL applies role/order/request/attempt scope,
expiry and the lower profile bounds before Python formats the result. Whole facts
are omitted when they cannot fit; values and source references are never truncated
or summarized. The lifetime setting caps a writer's requested TTL and cannot
extend an existing shorter retention policy. Canonical facts remain available to
the trusted stale-result fence even if the model sees a text or JSON projection.

SQL wrappers retain the original public function identities and call private typed
implementations. Agent identities cannot execute those private helpers to bypass
the selected profile. Validation covers Python definitions and frozen database
bindings. Historical agents without a profile keep their previous behavior.

Sources: [memory profile and projections](../src/delivery/memory_profiles.py),
[database profile enforcement](../sql/migrations/024_agent_memory_modes.sql),
[profile and isolation checks](../tests/test_memory_profiles.py).

## What a memory is

A memory is a row in PostgreSQL's `agent_memory_facts`, with typed identity and
scope columns and a `body` stored as JSONB. It is not a CSV, a separate file per
agent or an unrestricted chat transcript. `agent_memory_types` holds the accepted
body schemas. The `agent_memory_current` view selects the latest revision.
The Anatomy storage tank renders a synthetic example for the selected role,
validates its body with the real schema, and formats each view with the actual
`project_memory` function. It never reads private run memory.

Scope (run, store/entity, role, context and subject) and history (row ID, version,
source event, observation time, expiry and previous revision) are server assigned.
`fact_id` in recall corresponds to the SQL row's `id`. Simulation seconds govern
expiry. One JSONB body can occupy at most 2,048 SQL-serialized bytes; this is
distinct from the whole recall envelope's 8 KiB limit. Role manifests separately
cap live entries and body bytes across the entity.

## Semantic recall and the core

The worker first gets canonical candidates through its fenced SQL recall.
Semantic mode embeds the query and those candidates locally using
`BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` (384 dimensions), then ranks only that authorized set.
Queries are bounded to 512 UTF-8 bytes and the candidate set to eight facts.
The SQL gate runs again after ranking: invented, foreign, stale or expired IDs
cannot become agent input. This costs two fenced memory reads, so both tool
slots must be available. Missing dependencies and invalid embeddings fail closed.

An ADK restaurant receives the selected projection through its scoped tool
response. Deterministic policies retain canonical facts for decision provenance;
selecting a profile does not turn them into model-driven agents. The customer
service classifier has fresh complaint sessions, no persistent recall contract,
and durable inference receipts for billing/idempotency. Its chaos turns see only
affected-order facts. Repeated customer complaints across different orders are
**not** supported by this memory scope.

The three checked-in recall cases exercise repeated reservation, stock refusal
and expiry within one order, against a no-memory baseline. Tests cover real local
embeddings/pgvector and isolation. Vertex HTTP payloads and filters use a mock;
there is no live Vertex quality benchmark or published memory-specific pass-rate,
latency or cost receipt. Audit includes backend, model, query hash and returned
fact IDs. Zero paid embedding API calls does not imply free infrastructure.

## Local and Google Cloud storage

Locally, Compose's `postgres-data` volume retains canonical facts. The optional
`agent_semantic_vectors` cache stores JSONB numeric arrays keyed by fact ID and
model; SQL casts them to pgvector for exact cosine ranking. It is not a global
unfiltered nearest-neighbor index.

The optional GCP live path keeps canonical facts in Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 17.
Cloud Run uses scoped database logins and role service accounts. Terraform requires
`active` and `enable_live` for storage, plus `live_ready` after migrations, logins
and secret versions before starting services.

With `enable_vector_search`, Vertex stores 384-number vectors, model-prefixed
fact IDs, opaque scope/model hashes and expiry metadata. No raw fact body or
query text is sent to Vertex; the query vector is sent. Embeddings are derived
data, and hashes are filters rather than encryption. The public-network endpoint
requires authenticated API calls through Application Default Credentials.
Terraform grants the configured api, restaurant and dispatcher identities
bounded index-update/query permissions.

Cloud SQL and the single-replica Vertex deployment have idle costs. The public
replay needs neither. `active=false` removes these resources; documentation never
starts them or claims a deployment is running. The lab Terraform currently
disables SQL backups and deletion protection. TTL removes recall eligibility,
not history or Vertex datapoints. There is no automatic Vertex TTL deletion or
archival pipeline. Teardown can remove retained audit data.

Implementation: [typed contracts](../src/delivery/typed_memory.py),
[generated public reference](../src/delivery/memory_reference.py),
[scoped runtime](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py),
[ADK tool projection](../src/delivery/adk_restaurant.py),
[typed SQL](../sql/migrations/015_typed_memory.sql),
[semantic interface](../src/delivery/semantic_memory.py),
[semantic SQL](../sql/migrations/031_semantic_memory.sql),
[Cloud SQL and live workers](../infra/production/live.tf),
[Vertex infrastructure](../infra/production/vector.tf),
[semantic tests](../tests/test_semantic_memory.py),
[recall cases](../evals/memory/recall.json).

## Historical profile verification

Verified 2026-10-29: 38 memory-profile checks passed, including all four views,
mixed-scope rejection, byte/fact bounds, TTL clamping, retained history, legacy
definition compatibility, frozen binding validation and denial of private SQL
helpers. The full local suite passed 553 tests, with Ruff, mypy over 49 modules,
host JavaScript syntax, twelve repeated role scenarios and six offline judge
cases. No paid calls are used by that suite. The separate live routing comparison
used typed recall in every arm; it does not compare memory-mode decision quality.

## Historical local verification

Verified 2026-10-28 (Europe/Madrid): the complete suite passed **307 tests**.
Ruff, JavaScript syntax and mypy over 36 source files passed. Tests use real
scoped Postgres identities to deny other orders, stores and roles, direct history
reads, forged sources, untyped fields, stale leases and budget resets. They also
check current-request recall, expiry without older-value resurrection, rejected
old snapshots, concurrent capacity admission and transactional ACK rollback.

A fresh two-order run delivered both meals through 48 events with zero dead
letters and zero model calls. It retained 42 typed revisions and recorded 26
recalled facts; each recalled source matched the decision owner and current order.
Stock invariants and all five replay projections matched. Browser checks covered
readable provenance/expiry, actual recalled values, the legacy 64-order history,
closed raw evidence, zero console errors and no horizontal overflow.
The [local receipt](evidence/typed-memory-local.json) records these counts. This is
a functional/isolation receipt, not a latency or decision-quality benchmark.

The default 64-order city also completed: 1,762 events, zero retries/dead letters
or model calls, 1,791 replay facts and matching projections/invariants. This check
first exposed live-memory pressure from closed supplier requests. The terminal
retention policy above fixed it without raising the 64-entry limit; a regression
test checks that expiry retains history and does not revive older reservations.
The deliberately scarce baseline still delivered seven meals and failed 57 on
supply/deadline constraints, with 21 open physical jobs and three late physical
deliveries retained in its evidence. This memory change does not improve those
business outcomes.

## Enterprise patterns informing the design

- [Google ADK session, state and memory separation](https://adk.dev/sessions/):
  separate a conversation's events and working state from searchable knowledge
  across conversations. Our order trace and private working records address the
  first part; cross-session knowledge remains to be built.
- [Google Agent Platform Memory Bank](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/memory-bank):
  identity-scoped retrieval, background extraction/consolidation, expiry and memory
  revisions are useful reference capabilities. We do not provision this service.
  A scope string alone is not authorization; IAM or database policy must enforce it.
- [LangGraph memory](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/concepts/memory):
  durable thread checkpoints and separately namespaced long-term stores. We use
  database transactions and events rather than importing its graph/checkpointer.
- [OpenAI context engineering with sessions](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/agents_sdk/session_memory):
  bounded recent turns and structured summaries help control context size. We
  have numeric budgets but do not yet compact or summarize agent conversations.

## Next slices

1. **Broader recall evaluation.** Extend the implemented three-case local
   semantic-recall comparison to more roles and measured model outcomes. Jev ingredient
   search is a separate capability, not a memory search engine. New fact schemas
   need reviewed migrations and compatibility tests, not edits to old records.
2. **Small handoff records.** Queue an explicit brief with the order, current
   commitments, custody, deadline, last verified observation and evidence links.
   Export only approved fields. A courier or supplier should not receive the
   sender's whole memory or another customer's conversation.
3. **Consolidation outside the critical path.** At order closure, derive useful
   facts such as observed supplier delays. Start with local rules. Any optional
   model summary needs its own budget, provenance, validation and expiry; it must
   not edit the agent's instructions or grant capabilities. Raw customer text
   remains untrusted data, including when recalled later.
4. **Publish memory evaluations.** Compare no-memory, typed working records,
   filtered recall and compact summaries on the same seeds. Measure task success,
   stale-fact errors, recovery correctness, retrieval latency, context size and
   model cost when explicitly enabled. Include expired stock, contradicted facts,
   duplicated events, interrupted writes, malicious complaints and cross-role
   retrieval attempts. Require zero unauthorized disclosure or inventory-policy
   violations; publish measured results rather than claiming framework parity.

The typed records and filtered recall are implemented; comparative performance
and decision-quality evaluations remain future work. A vector database or larger
context window by itself would not demonstrate better memory.

# Local agent foundation and optional GCP portability

Original design: 2026-10-23; implementation clarifications: 2026-10-28. Default city
development remains local, without provider calls or cloud credentials. The optional
Cloud Run/Vertex recovery judge has since been implemented and live-verified;
Google ADK and a fully cloud-hosted business runtime remain proposed adapters.
Use [the exact implementation](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md),
[current GCP inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md) and
[enterprise decisions](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md) for the current source-reviewed contract.

The inventory implementation is now available: see [implemented foundation](AGENT-FOUNDATION.md)
for actual modules, permissions, budgets and verification. The proposed ADK-specific
shape and example contract below remain future design, not the executable role schema.

## What an agent is in this project

An agent is a versioned identity with a goal, a bounded decision loop, observations,
permitted actions and durable accountability. Its lifecycle is:

claim event -> verify authenticated scope -> commit durable attempt/tool allowance
-> prepare/invoke/save outside effects transaction if enabled -> begin fenced effects transaction -> load
permitted facts/memory -> decide and execute permitted tools -> record outcome,
memory and outgoing events -> commit those effects and ACK atomically.

A prompt or SOUL.md supplies behavioral guidance. It does not provide security,
durability, memory isolation, approvals or cost enforcement. A deterministic policy
and an ADK reasoning policy should both fit the same event and tool contracts, so
the experiment can measure whether model judgment helps.

## Researched Google options (not a deployment choice)

| Option | Documented capability | Project judgment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADK on Cloud Run | Open-source agent framework with local and cloud deployment. Cloud Run has services for request-driven work, worker pools for continuous queue consumers and jobs for finite tasks. | Deferred portability candidate after local acceptance. Research suggests explicit control over our queue contract and a shared image; jobs, worker pools and services are possible future adapters, not current implementation requirements. |
| Managed Agent Runtime | Managed agent deployment, scaling, security and framework integration. Current docs place it under Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform; ReasoningEngine remains an API resource name for compatibility. | Keep as a deployment adapter option when managed operations justify it. It does not replace business transactions, queue semantics or our scoped memory experiment. |
| Managed Agents API | Config-driven autonomous agents in sandbox environments; launch stage and data-handling terms need review for the chosen feature/version. | Evaluate only on synthetic fixtures first; private Bakiano exports are outside the current approved model data contract. |
| ADK Agent Config | Version-sensitive configuration-based role/workflow assembly. | Preserve our small validated role contract and use a future adapter over tested, pinned ADK APIs; framework configuration is not the durable authorization contract. |

Sources: [ADK overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/adk),
[Cloud Run resource choices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/ai-agents),
[Agent Runtime](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime),
[Managed Agents API and restrictions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/managed-agents),
[experimental Agent Config](https://adk.dev/agents/config/).

These links preserve research, not a selected deployment or a dependency of the local
lab. Benchmark the same role/tools against a rules-only baseline locally.
Pin a tested ADK/SDK version and model version in implementation; do not use a moving
latest alias in scored runs. Verify regional availability, quotas and pricing before
deploying. No cloud resources or paid model calls were created by this research.

## Reuse the implementation, specialize the role

Proposed repository shape:

```text
agent_runtime/
  factory.py          # role config -> deterministic or ADK decision policy
  worker.py           # queue lease, deadline, bounded loop, commit/ACK
  context.py          # authoritative reads, redaction, scoped memory retrieval
  tools.py            # fixed tool registry and schema validation
  budgets.py          # durable reservation before inference/tool expense
  telemetry.py        # event/decision/model/tool spans and sanitized records
  transports/         # Postgres first; cloud notification adapter later
config/agents/
  inventory/role.json
  inventory/SOUL.md
  dispatcher/role.json
  dispatcher/SOUL.md
  director/role.json
  director/SOUL.md
config/topologies/    # reporting/approval routes, separate from role behavior
```

These proposed paths describe a future reasoning adapter layout. The implemented
inventory foundation uses `src/delivery/agent_runtime.py`, `agent_access.py` and
`agent_specs.py`, plus the inventory role/soul paths shown above.
Build and validate one shared factory locally, with deterministic policies and scripted
model adapters. ADK is optional behind these contracts; default demos make no provider
calls. ADK packaging and cloud business-worker hosting remain proposed; the bounded
Cloud Run/Vertex judge and its standalone Terraform root are already implemented.
Copy a role configuration and soul file, not the worker implementation. Instantiate
inventory roles with store-specific scope. Configuration is developer-controlled,
immutable during a run, validated at startup and hashed into every decision record.
Event payloads cannot choose a new soul, tools, identity or broader scope.

Example project role contract (illustrative, not directly executable ADK config):

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "role": "inventory",
  "version": "1",
  "soul": "SOUL.md",
  "objective": "Report stock truthfully and propose feasible replenishment",
  "decision_policy": "rules-first-adk-on-exception",
  "scope": {"store_ids": ["store-1"]},
  "accepts": ["basket.requested", "availability.requested", "stock.shortage"],
  "emits": ["inventory.decided", "replenishment.proposed", "approval.requested"],
  "tools": ["inventory.read", "inventory.reserve", "replenishment.propose"],
  "memory": {"namespace": "run/role/store", "retention": "scenario-defined"},
  "model_policy": "budgeted-exception-model-v1",
  "limits": {"model_calls_per_event": 1, "tool_steps_per_event": 6},
  "budget_policy": "inventory-run-budget-v1",
  "output_schema": "inventory-decision-v1",
  "deadline_policy": "inventory-deadlines-v1",
  "escalation_route": "topology.inventory.supervisor"
}
```

Budget/model/deadline references resolve to trusted versioned policies with numeric
caps. The tool list is intersected with server-side policy for the authenticated
principal; editing JSON cannot grant new authority. In a future reasoning adapter,
trusted SOUL text can guide model decisions within that authority. Current local
policies do not interpret SOUL, and the GCP gateway uses its own fixed prompt rather
than the local role SOUL. Neither can raise budgets or remove approval requirements.

Example inventory soul:

> Protect stock accuracy and explain uncertainty. Read authoritative availability
> before making a promise. Separate confirmed units from expected receipts. Prefer
> deterministic tools for stock arithmetic. Propose alternatives only within verified
> compatibility and customer consent. Escalate requests outside your store or authority.

## Local sample data

Target ten daily Bakiano sample dates: 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-23 inclusive.
October 13 through October 23 inclusive would be eleven dates. Keep dated snapshots
local, with source identity, actual observation timestamps, provenance and hashes.
Only label a date observed when authentic source data establishes it; list missing
days explicitly. Never invent historical prices or relabel a current observation as
a past one. Synthetic fallback rows must be clearly marked and cannot fill an
observed-history claim.

## Isolation and data leakage

- Share the container image across roles, but deploy different authority boundaries
  with different workload identities, database roles and tool permissions. Two ADK
  objects in one process do not establish IAM isolation.
- Resolve store/run scope from trusted deployment configuration and authenticated
  tool context. Do not trust a store ID supplied by the model as authorization.
- Give agents narrow projections of catalogue and order facts, not the full Bakiano
  checkout, warehouse account, source credentials or another role's transcript.
- Keep provider credentials in workload identity/secret facilities, never prompts,
  memory documents, event payloads or traces. Avoid downloaded long-lived service
  account keys. Review granted identity defaults rather than assuming no access.
- Separate transient reasoning context, scoped episodes and canonical state. Filter
  memory access before retrieval, not by asking the model to ignore unauthorized hits.
- Treat complaints, product text and retrieved episodes as untrusted data. Enforce
  allowed actions in tools; record injection rejection without propagating secrets.

Google's managed Agent Identity is associated with the deployed runtime resource;
arbitrary role names within one deployment do not automatically get distinct
identities. Agent Gateway provides governance over approved destinations and tools.
These complement, rather than replace, store-level business authorization.
Sources: [Agent Identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/agent-identity),
[Agent Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview).

## Queues, state and execution boundaries

Keep Postgres as the authoritative business store and durable event queue initially.
GCP can host it in Cloud SQL, subject to deployment/extension checks. The local Docker
backend remains the offline reference. Current memory uses typed facts and exact
SQL filters. Any future pgvector adapter must be a separately evaluated scoped
memory mode so comparisons do not silently switch memory systems.

For persistent workers, Cloud Run worker pools can consume the existing queue. For
finite experiments, a run-to-completion job can drive the simulation. Do not move
the current API background-task controller unchanged onto a request-billed service.
Durable controller ownership/checkpoints and restart recovery must precede claims
of cloud fault tolerance.

If adopting Pub/Sub later, select and document one transport contract. An outbox
relay may send durable wakeups while Postgres retains priority, simulated due-time
and idempotency semantics. If Pub/Sub becomes the actual transport, add a transactional
inbox/outbox and explicitly reimplement/test these semantics. Do not claim Pub/Sub
natively provides our priority queue or simulation clock.

All role-to-role cooperation stays queued. Do not wire ADK AgentTool, direct agent
transfer, shared conversational state or A2A calls around this ledger. A supervisor
requests another role's work with a correlated event; the result is another event.

ADK trigger endpoints can process Pub/Sub/Eventarc requests, but redelivery creates
another session and default in-memory sessions are ephemeral. Deduplicate with the
business event ID, not an ADK session ID. Pub/Sub exactly-once is regional and pull-only;
it does not establish exactly-once business effects or external model billing.
Sources: [ambient agents](https://adk.dev/runtime/ambient-agents/),
[Pub/Sub delivery guarantees](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/exactly-once-delivery).

Implemented for the optional judge: model calls run outside worker database
connections. A fenced request snapshots scoped facts, local proposal, recall and
identity. Before dispatch, current context/time/recall and remaining tool slots
are checked; a single-dispatch marker and call/token allowance commit first.
Structured results are saved separately. A fresh effects transaction revalidates
the snapshot before applying domain effects, memory, outgoing events and ACK
atomically. Reclaimed events reuse saved results without another call. An uncertain
dispatch fails closed rather than automatically spending again. Legacy calls
without a compatible durable snapshot are also denied without resend.
See [durable inference](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md). Gateway-wide monetary admission,
supervisor recovery and distributed tracing remain enterprise follow-up work.

## Next implementation gate

Before adding more reasoning roles:

1. Implemented for eight role kinds: strict schema, fixed tools and shared factory;
   deterministic policies are the default and the optional GCP judge is bounded.
2. Real non-superuser tests exercise store/run/role/order/request/attempt isolation;
   twelve local role scenarios now have explicit scores and repeated receipts.
3. Add an ADK reasoning adapter only behind the tested event/tool contracts; keep
   routine city development independent of cloud deployments and inference.
4. Extend adversarial tests for every new model/tool integration; prompts cannot
   grant tools, memory, spending or approval authority, and cooperation stays queued.
5. Replace the in-process controller with durable ownership and checkpoints. Kill
   controller and worker separately and demonstrate local recovery from both.
6. Preserve sample provenance, explicit missing days and the local baseline while
   separately evaluating any paid cloud decision or proposed hosting change.

## Deferred ADK and cloud-worker adapters

The existing standalone Terraform root, keyless Cloud Run judge and start/status/
stop commands are implemented; they do not host the city, business workers or
memory in GCP. ADK, managed agent hosting, cloud business storage and broader
governance remain separate proposed changes. Preserve the shared contracts and
prove reliability/cost gates before adopting them. No deployment or provider call
is required by routine local development or by this documentation review.

# Durable inference without open database transactions

The optional recovery judge uses three committed phases: prepare a request,
invoke and save a result, then apply it against fresh authoritative state. The
network call has no open worker database connection or transaction. Local rules,
role scope, leases and business constraints remain the execution authority.

This chapter describes the new local request/result protocol. It does not deploy
GCP resources or demonstrate live model quality. Crash verification uses a fake
provider and real worker-process termination; no paid calls are needed.

## Execution and transaction boundaries

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Scoped judge worker
    participant D as PostgreSQL
    participant P as Bounded provider
    A->>D: Prepare immutable request under fenced lease
    D-->>A: Commit request, context and local proposal
    A->>D: Commit dispatch marker and call allowance
    Note over A,D: Close connection before remote I/O
    A->>P: Invoke with sanitized numeric facts
    P-->>A: Schema-validated verdict
    A->>D: Save result in a short fenced transaction
    D-->>A: Commit saved result
    A->>D: Re-read current state and validate saved proposal
    Note over A,D: Apply effects, memory, outbox and ACK atomically
    D-->>A: Commit completed event
```

The preparatory snapshot comes from the authenticated incoming event, the judge's
scoped tools and selective memory recall. It includes a locally computed courier
and route proposal. The durable record binds that input to its run, namespace,
source event, frozen role definition and endpoint. The cloud receives only the
existing numeric allowlist and the number of recalled facts; memory bodies,
customer names, local identifiers and raw route coordinates remain local.

Before dispatch admission, the worker rechecks context, simulated time and recalled
facts. It also verifies enough tool slots remain for the fresh recall and five
application operations. Known-stale preparation is denied before spending a call.
After the dispatch marker commits, all worker SQL connections are closed. Token
acquisition and the provider request happen outside the transaction. A separate
short transaction saves the validated response. `Queue.process` then starts its
usual effects transaction, reloads the authoritative event, validates its fence,
reads current business state and consumes the saved result. The deterministic
policy does not call the provider from inside this transaction.

## Recovery policy

| Durable state at restart | Recovery | Additional provider call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prepared, dispatch not claimed | A live fenced worker may claim dispatch | One admitted call |
| In flight under another still-active worker | Leave ownership intact; report busy | None |
| Dispatch committed, previous worker died | Record an unknown outcome and fail closed after reclaim | None |
| Response received but result not saved | Outcome remains unknown after worker death | None |
| Validated result saved, effects not committed | Reuse the saved result and revalidate current facts | None |
| Effects transaction crashed before commit | Roll back effects, memory, outgoing events and ACK; reuse result on reclaim | None |
| Applied and acknowledged | Work is complete; a stale worker cannot apply again | None |
| Legacy call with no durable snapshot | Preserve its allowance and deny; old inputs cannot be proven compatible | None |

Prepared requests and saved results are keyed by the source event, not by a queue
delivery attempt. Reclaiming an event therefore does not create a second model
call or reserve a second model allowance. A genuinely new decision event remains
a separate admission. Reservations for uncertain calls are retained.

An approval is a proposal about the saved facts. The application phase rechecks
the current job, delivery attempt, custody, courier availability, route and
deadline. A stale or incompatible proposal is rejected. The model cannot invent
a replacement route or override the SQL feasibility gates.

## What safe retries can and cannot mean

There is no distributed transaction between PostgreSQL and a model provider.
The worker cannot distinguish a crash immediately before sending from a crash
after the provider accepted the request but before its response was recorded.
A stable local request key does not prove provider-side deduplication or
exactly-once billing. The implementation deliberately avoids automatic resend
across this uncertain boundary.

This policy trades availability for bounded spend and safe business effects.
Unknown outcomes require a denial or an explicit future reconciliation workflow;
they are not silently retried until an answer arrives. A future provider that
offers an idempotent request API and durable result lookup could support a
different recovery policy, after its behavior and billing semantics are tested.

## Isolation, budgets and evidence

Raw request and history tables are not agent-readable. Narrow SQL functions
derive scope from `session_user`, require the current event lease and budget
ticket, and fence dispatch/result/application transitions. A stale worker cannot
overwrite a newer terminal outcome. Recorded errors use safe codes, not provider
exception messages that might contain credentials.

The original per-run model call and token limits still apply. Dispatch admission
charges a request once; reusing its saved result does not charge another call.
This remains a call/token allowance, not a project-wide currency cap. The
existing GCP gateway and Terraform resources do not change for this local work.

The [crash suite](../tests/test_inference_crash_recovery.py) checks physical process
death at the phase boundaries, saved-result
reuse, uncertain-outcome denial, lease fencing, concurrent ownership, unchanged
business effects and the absence of worker SQL transactions during provider I/O.
Use the [health dashboard](HEALTH.md) for fresh source-linked test evidence and
[architecture decisions](ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md) for the remaining trade-offs.
The implementation lives in [durable_inference.py](../src/delivery/durable_inference.py),
the [new SQL state machine](../sql/migrations/016_durable_inference.sql),
the [shared worker](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py) and
[receipt-only policy](../src/delivery/fleet_policy.py).

# A2A agents over the durable queue

The running application exposes two real A2A 1.0 JSON-RPC servers using the
official Python SDK 1.3.0. Each publishes a discoverable Agent Card:

| Agent | Card on localhost:8010 | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dispatcher | `/a2a/dispatcher/.well-known/agent-card.json` | Dispatch pending Madrid-baseline orders with the existing road/energy/shift policy. |
| Customer service | `/a2a/customer_service/.well-known/agent-card.json` | Classify an existing complaint with the scripted Google ADK model and enforce the existing refund approval policy. |

The request is a text part containing JSON with `run_id` and `entity_id`. An
entity must already exist in that run. The adapter publishes (or reuses) the
canonical durable event, claims a fenced lease, and invokes the existing role
handler. It processes at most 32 eligible events per request. Concurrent work or
backoff can return a `ready` or `leased` queue state; only `done` means the event
has committed. An assigned delivery still requires the simulation clock to
advance its courier. The adapter does not fabricate physical completion.

```bash
make setup
curl http://localhost:8010/a2a/dispatcher/.well-known/agent-card.json
python3 scripts/call_a2a.py dispatcher RUN_UUID ORDER_ID
python3 scripts/call_a2a.py customer_service RUN_UUID COMPLAINT_ID
```

Use identifiers from `/api/state` or a seeded baseline run. These endpoints wrap
the Madrid-baseline dispatcher and customer service, not the separate inventory
lab's scoped fleet. The client uses `A2ACardResolver`, `ClientFactory`, and
`SendMessageRequest`, including protocol version negotiation. Raw JSON-RPC
clients must send `A2A-Version: 1.0`. A response contains the queue event ID,
attempt count, domain outcome, and `paid_calls_this_request: 0`.

Customer inference is explicitly pinned to the offline ADK adapter even if the
host has a paid provider configured. Scripted advice uses `adk_offline`, so the
existing refund gate asks for human approval and never grants a refund based on
fixture output. Repeating an entity request reuses its event and cached model
receipt; it does not reserve a second inference call. No model or SQL tool calls
are accepted from a client.

This is a local demonstration: Compose binds port 8010 to loopback; the adapter
also checks Host/Origin and caps the streamed HTTP body at 8 KiB. The immediate
A2A Message workflow is advertised without streaming or push notifications.
Business work survives process restarts in PostgreSQL; no durable A2A task store
is claimed. An internet deployment requires authentication, tenant-to-run
authorization, ingress limits, and a reviewed public Agent Card.

Implementation: [server and queue adapter](../src/delivery/a2a_server.py),
[SDK client](../scripts/call_a2a.py), and
[protocol plus real-agent integration tests](../tests/test_a2a_server.py).
Tests discover both cards and call both servers using the real SDK over ASGI;
the integration case checks actual courier assignment, ADK advice, refund
escalation, and replay with one durable zero-dollar reservation.

Official references checked on 2026-10-29:
[A2A Python SDK](https://a2aproject.github.io/a2a-python/) and
[server tutorial](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/tutorials/python/5-start-server/).
The installed 1.3 SDK uses protobuf message types; pre-1.0 Pydantic examples
are not used here.
