# Enterprise agents on GCP: architecture and delivery decisions

Reviewed against source and Google documentation on **2026-10-28**. This is the
client architecture guide. [Agent implementation](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md) explains
the exact executable worker; [GCP components](GCP-COMPONENTS.md) inventories every
declared cloud resource; [GCP operations](GCP-AI.md) covers start/status/stop.
Recommendations below are **proposed** unless explicitly marked implemented.
This review did not deploy infrastructure, inspect credentials or invoke a model.

## Client objective and current decision

Build a delivery/sourcing system whose agents can make bounded decisions while
inventory, consent, custody, approvals and money remain enforceable business rules.
Use the local synthetic city as a reproducible client test environment. Introduce
paid inference only for a declared decision task and promote it only when measured
benefit exceeds added latency, failures and cost.

Implemented today: custom Python/Postgres role workers, queued cooperation,
authenticated scopes, typed selective recall, budgets and local scenario evals.
The optional cloud component is an IAM-authenticated **Cloud Run recovery judge
calling a Google publisher model through Vertex REST**. It can veto a locally
computed candidate; it cannot invent a route, change stock or execute a delivery.
The [restaurant adapter](ADK-RESTAURANT.md) now runs Google ADK locally with granular
tools and an explicitly offline model double. Managed Agent Runtime, Memory Bank
and Agent Gateway are not deployed; restaurant Gemini calls are not enabled.

Google's current product documentation uses **Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform**
and **Agent Runtime**; older Agent Engine/Vertex AI names and API resource names
remain visible in documentation and integrations. Separate the framework, hosting,
model API and governance layers when choosing components. Google documents both
Cloud Run and managed runtime options; our selection depends on the client's
operational and governance requirements, not a requirement to use every service.
[Google architecture component guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/choose-agentic-ai-architecture-components).

## Choose the runtime by workload

Before platform selection, agree the task and unsafe outcomes, expected demand,
deadline/latency SLO, acceptable cost per successful task, tenant/data boundaries,
processing region, retention, operator approval rules and RTO/RPO. Assign owners
for policy, data access, release approval, incident response and billing. The local
city supplies test incidents; it does not define an enterprise client's SLOs.

| Option | Use when | Our decision / limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloud Run service | Bounded, stateless HTTP decisions; variable demand; explicit container/network controls | Implemented for the judge, with local durable inference phases. Candidate for a separately evaluated ADK pilot |
| Cloud Run job | Finite evaluations, imports or migrations | Proposed for an explicitly cloud-enabled benchmark; current benchmark stays local |
| Cloud Run worker pool | Continuous pull consumers without an inbound HTTP API | Candidate for production queue workers; provisioned instance lifetime is billable |
| Managed Agent Runtime | Managed agent hosting, sessions, identity/governance and lifecycle capabilities materially reduce client operations | Evaluate against the same workload and permissions before choosing it |
| GKE | Client already needs Kubernetes-specific networking, scheduling or isolation controls | No current requirement; owning a cluster is not an agent prerequisite |

Cloud Run services can scale to zero; jobs and worker pools have different
lifecycle/billing behavior. Moving an in-process API background task onto a
request-billed service does not make it a durable worker. Choose a supervised
consumer or a bounded task, with external state and restart-safe ownership.
[Cloud Run agent resource choices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/ai-agents),
[billing behavior](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/billing-settings).

The local restaurant implementation pins ADK 2.13.0 and compatible SDK dependencies.
Keep our role definition, authenticated tool boundary and queue protocol as the
business contract; ADK becomes the reasoning adapter. Do not replace those
contracts with a prompt or a framework's implicit shared state. Google's
[ADK and Cloud Run reference architecture](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/single-agent-ai-system-adk-cloud-run)
provides a deployment reference; it is not a claim that this repository already
implements that architecture.

## A reusable enterprise agent contract

The proposed reasoning adapter should accept a validated definition containing
purpose, role/version, instructions, supported event schemas, tool references,
memory policy, numeric limits, deadline behavior and escalation route. Tenant/run
scope comes from a trusted deployment/event binding. Configurations and model
proposals cannot choose arbitrary URLs, credentials, recipients or tools.

Construct one adapter for one trust boundary: load frozen definition → resolve
approved tool wrappers → build scoped context → invoke bounded reasoning →
validate output → request domain execution. Reuse the image/factory and change
approved definitions. Adding a new role still requires domain permissions and
evaluation coverage. Several ADK subagents in one process do not receive distinct
IAM identities merely because their prompts have different names.

Domain tool endpoints must authenticate the workload and independently authorize
tenant, role, current order and operation. For MCP or A2A, implement authenticated,
schema-versioned adapters; accepted business messages become durable queue events.
Do not add direct agent transfer/shared conversational state that bypasses the
project's queue-only cooperation rule. Tool calls to a domain service and messages
to another agent are different operations. Google's safety guidance reinforces
enforcement in tool context/callbacks rather than relying on instructions alone.
[ADK safety and security](https://adk.dev/safety/).

## Identity, isolation and governance

**Implemented:** separate caller and runtime service accounts; caller-specific
Cloud Run invocation; a custom runtime role with only
`aiplatform.endpoints.predict`; keyless ADC/impersonation; scoped PostgreSQL agent
logins. The endpoint is internet-reachable with IAM authentication. There is no
private VPC ingress or generic tenant authorization gateway in the current module.

**For a client deployment:** separate dev/staging/production ownership and state,
deployer and runtime identities, and role trust boundaries. Reject public
invocation. Decide ingress/egress, residency, key management, incident access and
retention with the client before selecting networking controls. Identity grants
permission to reach a service; business authorization still decides which store,
order, event lease and operation the caller may access.

For restricted client data, assess private connectivity and VPC Service Controls
against supported services/locations; a perimeter complements IAM to reduce
exfiltration risk. Select CMEK only where supported and required. Test denied
egress and approved access explicitly. An EU-hosted Cloud Run service using a
global model endpoint is not an EU-only processing guarantee. These controls are
proposed, with no network perimeter or CMEK resource in the current module.
[VPC Service Controls](https://cloud.google.com/security/vpc-service-controls).

When choosing managed Agent Runtime, evaluate **Agent Identity** rather than
assuming a shared default service account is sufficiently narrow. Its identity is
tied to the deployed runtime resource, not every local role object. Current docs
describe runtime-bound credentials and default grants including
`roles/aiplatform.agentDefaultAccess` and `roles/aiplatform.agentContextEditor`;
review those grants and keep context-aware credential protections enabled.
These features are not retroactively provided by our existing Cloud Run service.
[Agent Identity behavior and defaults](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/agent-identity).

For governed tool estates, evaluate **Agent Registry**, **Agent Gateway** and
**Model Armor** against the chosen runtime and client policy. Registry describes
approved agents/tools; gateway enforcement and content inspection complement
IAM and domain authorization. They do not make untrusted tool output safe by
definition. Confirm runtime support, launch stage, region, pricing and Terraform
coverage before adoption; include allow/deny and injection tests in acceptance.
No such resources are currently provisioned.
[Agent platform layers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/agents),
[gateway deployment options](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview).

Terraform ownership is an adoption gate for each proposed service. Verify that the
selected provider/API can create, import, plan, update and delete the runtime and
its dependent billable resources. An SDK or ADK CLI deployment is not automatically
Terraform-owned. Defer an unsupported component or design a reviewed declarative
lifecycle module; document session/memory data retention and cleanup separately.

Use Workload Identity Federation for production CI/external workloads instead of
downloaded service-account keys or a human ADC mount. Bind federation to the
approved repository/workflow/environment and trusted claims, and separate plan
from approved apply permissions. The current GitHub workflow tests local Docker;
it is not a cloud deployment pipeline. For third-party secrets, introduce Secret
Manager only with narrow access and lifecycle ownership; Gemini on GCP needs
workload credentials, not a hard-coded model API key.
[Google pipeline identity guidance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/best-practices-for-using-service-accounts-in-deployment-pipelines),
[federation setup](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines).

## Durable execution: implemented local phases and remaining gaps

The local worker atomically commits state, memory, decision, outbox and ACK.
The optional judge now uses a separate durable request/result protocol:

1. In a short fenced transaction, save the authenticated event, scoped observations,
   relevant recall, frozen identity and local proposal as an immutable request.
2. Commit a single-dispatch marker and call/token admission, then close the worker
   database connection before authentication or provider I/O.
3. Save a validated result in its own short transaction. Reclaiming the same event
   reuses that result. A crash with an in-flight outcome fails closed rather than
   resending: the provider does not offer a proven exactly-once billing contract.
4. In the effects transaction, re-read current state and compare the saved facts,
   proposal, recall and time. SQL independently rechecks feasibility; effects,
   memory, outgoing events and ACK commit together or roll back together.

See [durable inference and crash boundaries](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md). This is a local
single-dispatch ledger, not a shared gateway-wide currency cap or a durable cloud
supervisor. Prepared work can resume; saved results can be reapplied safely;
uncertain invocations retain their charge and need explicit reconciliation rather
than hidden retries. Future distributed completion wakeups and tracing propagation
must preserve the same queue-only contract.

Add durable controller ownership/checkpoints and an orphan-identity reaper.
Kill the controller and the inference worker separately; prove recovery before
claiming cloud fault tolerance. Move state to Cloud SQL only after testing actual
managed-Postgres migration privileges, non-owner RLS, extensions, pooling,
connection limits, backup/restore and failover. Local superuser provisioning is
not evidence that unchanged migrations work in a managed service.

If Pub/Sub is added, start with wakeups from a transactional outbox while SQL
retains priority, virtual due time and domain idempotency. A full transport change
requires an inbox/outbox design and new failure tests. Pub/Sub's exactly-once
feature is regional and pull-subscription-specific; it does not provide an atomic
transaction with our stock tables or exactly-once external model charging.
[Pub/Sub delivery semantics](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/exactly-once-delivery).

## Canonical state, sessions and memory

| Layer | Current implementation | Client design rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business truth | Transactional PostgreSQL stock/orders/consent/custody | SQL constraints and version checks remain authoritative |
| Conversation/session | Correlated queued order/call events and frozen run settings | Persist outside a scaled stateless runtime; derive user/tenant identity from authentication |
| Selective recall | Typed facts scoped to role/current order; request/attempt filters; provenance/expiry/history | Authorization filters precede retrieval; bound bytes and recall cost |
| Cross-session knowledge | Not implemented | Evaluate managed Memory Bank or a scoped PostgreSQL/vector design only for a measurable task |
| Audit | Decision/tool/memory receipts and replay facts | Separate agent recall access from operator audit access and retention |

Managed sessions and Memory Bank can reduce custom context management, but neither
replaces transactional business state. A scope label or semantic match is not an
authorization check. Evaluate extraction quality, poisoned/stale facts, consent,
deletion/export, region and metering before sending client history to a managed
memory service. Our cloud judge currently receives a **memory count**, not memories.
[Memory Bank capabilities](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/memory-bank).

Current TTL expires recall eligibility, not physical audit retention. Production
needs a declared wall-clock retention/deletion policy for facts, revisions, traces,
backups and model context. Add vector recall only if exact structured retrieval
fails a held-out task; then compare recall quality, leakage, latency and tokens.

## Model choice and cost controls

The historically verified model is `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`; Terraform requires an
explicit model/location, and the gateway assumes `MINIMAL` thinking is supported.
Do not swap in a newer model family without checking generation settings, regional
support, release status and rerunning the same evals. Record returned model version,
image/prompt/schema/role/fixture hashes, location and pricing date. Monitor model
retirement. A model alias is not a guarantee of identical future outputs.
[Model specifications and lifecycle](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/3-5-flash-lite).

Choose the least expensive model that passes the client's quality and latency
gates. For this numeric feasibility task, deterministic rules may remain the best
choice: the LLM's business benefit is unproven. A future ambiguous substitution or
incident-review task needs an approved evidence contract and human-calibrated
rubric before a larger model is justified.

Current standard global text rates checked 2026-10-28 for 3.5 Flash-Lite are $0.30
input and $2.50 output/reasoning per million tokens. At the caller's 8,192 + 256
reserved-token envelope, one illustrative maximum-envelope generation is
`(8192 × 0.30 + 256 × 2.50) / 1,000,000 = $0.0030976`; six are $0.0185856.
This is arithmetic for that SKU/location, **not a project-wide cost ceiling**.
It excludes compute, storage, logs, network, other clients and uncertain requests.
A local timeout or gateway 502 can follow a successful billable Vertex response.
[Current model pricing](https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing).

Before exposing more callers, add a **durable gateway admission ledger** keyed by
tenant/project/window and business request ID. Reserve worst-case gross currency,
input/output/reasoning tokens and calls before inference; reject exhaustion and
reconcile actual usage. Account for the complete prompt/schema/context and every
attempt, including auth/SDK retry behavior. Current local `model_usd: 0`, Cloud Run
maximum instances and per-run call reservations do not implement this ledger.

Configure actual/forecast billing alerts and a tested containment action, with
an owner for reconciliation. Budget alerts are not an immediate spending cap.
Current Google documentation also lists service-scoped spend-cap budgets for
Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) and Cloud Run, among eligible services. Assess
eligibility and manage separate project/service caps in Terraform before enabling
them. They are not deployed here. Enforcement is not instant; in-flight requests
and reporting latency can produce payable overages. They are not an all-project
ceiling. Use admission controls and explicit shutdown alongside billing signals.
[Google budget behavior](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets),
[Spend-cap scope and limitations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-spend-caps).

## Evals, observability and release gates

The current [local role battery](AGENT-EVALS.md) records 12/12 cases and 49/49
criteria across two matching seed-731 runs, plus 392 passing tests. It exercises
rules-based agents and scoped SQL identities. The separate historical live GCP
eval achieved 6/6 system cases with **one model answer and five preflight denials**;
an earlier missing-facts model approval is retained in the evidence. Neither is
a held-out model benchmark or proof of business uplift.

For a client, evaluate both final task success and the tool trajectory. Use a
frozen family-separated tuning/holdout split, repeat model cases, and compare
rules-only vs model-assisted runs on the same incident schedules. A second LLM may
help assess explanations with human calibration; it cannot replace the hard
feasibility/tenancy oracle. Check the launch stage and price of the selected
managed evaluation feature before using it in a contractual release process.
[Google agent evaluation dimensions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/evaluation-agents).

| Release gate | Evidence required before production |
| --- | --- |
| Isolation/safety | Zero executed hard-rule violations or cross-scope disclosures in declared adversarial cases; rejected attempts remain visible |
| Decision quality | Approve/deny confusion matrix, false denials, explanation support and human-reviewed disagreements on held-out incidents |
| Business outcome | Paired on-time delivery/recovery, abandoned work and operator effort, with predeclared tolerances and uncertainty |
| Performance | End-to-end cold/warm p50/p95/p99, queue age, timeout/429/5xx rates and late-result rejection against client deadline slack |
| Cost | Actual usage and gross currency per decision/successful recovery, uncertain reservations and concurrent admission tests |
| Recovery | Worker/controller failure, duplicate delivery, stale proposal, restore and rollback drills |
| Reproducibility | Frozen inputs, source/model/prompt/role versions, policy and architecture assignment, sanitized trace/eval receipts |

Add OpenTelemetry spans linking order → event → worker → tool → model, exported to
Cloud Trace/Logging/Monitoring with explicit redaction, sampling and retention.
Track budget admission, safety denials, feasible retries incorrectly denied,
queue/dead-letter growth and on-time delivery; an always-deny model can have perfect
uptime. Gateway stdout and local event inspection exist; complete distributed
tracing, alert policies and cloud eval dashboards do not.
Google describes observability and governance as distinct platform responsibilities.
[Agent platform architecture](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/agents).

## Terraform, delivery and shutdown ownership

Keep this client's root/state separate from Scrapmarket. Pin providers, Python
dependencies, base/deployable image digests and approved release provenance. The
current Dockerfile's base tag is mutable, even though deployed images use digests.
Add a reviewed CI plan/apply flow with federation, restricted deployer permissions and
protected production approval. Artifact provenance/scanning and rollback are
release work, not guarantees supplied by an image digest alone.

The demo currently uses ignored **local state**. A multi-operator enterprise
deployment should use an access-controlled remote backend, locking/versioned
recovery and separate environment states. Google's Cloud Storage backend pattern
is an appropriate candidate. A retained state bucket has storage cost and should
live outside an ephemeral runtime's teardown dependency chain; approve that cost
exception before introducing it. It is not currently provisioned.
[Google Terraform state guidance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/terraform/resource-management/store-state).

Current daily stop preserves project/APIs/IAM, removes billable gateway/image
resources and then unlinks billing. Protected project deletion is deliberately
blocked. Any new SQL database, memory store, secret, log sink or evaluation artifact
store needs Terraform ownership, startup/stop behavior, retention and verification.
An enterprise client's HA/backup/retention requirements can impose a persistent
cost floor; the local city's zero-cloud-cost development mode remains available.

## Delivery sequence and client demonstration

| Step | Scope | Acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Preserve local baseline | Versioned roles, business rules, queues and scenarios | Current isolation/regression receipts remain reproducible without credentials |
| 2. Harden paid decisions | Local durable request/result phases implemented; next: gateway-wide monetary admission and supervisor recovery | Local crash/duplicate/timeout checks plus future measured p95 and controller recovery; no double business effect |
| 3. Pilot one ADK role | Same approved tools and role contract, smallest passing model, explicit deployment identity | Same safety suite plus held-out quality/latency/cost comparison |
| 4. Select GCP hosting/governance | Cloud Run or managed runtime; networking, identity, memory and Terraform coverage based on client constraints | Reviewed threat/data-flow model, least-privilege negative tests and complete stop/retention inventory |
| 5. Operate and promote | Shadow evaluation, explicitly assigned canary, rollback and incident ownership | Agreed business/quality/SLO/cost gates and a signed-off handover |

In a walkthrough, show one order's queue lineage, authenticated scope, reservation,
selective memory, physical handoff and eval result. Then show the optional GCP
request boundary, caller/runtime identities, actual model-vs-policy response and
usage. Finish with the Terraform plan/parked status and the gaps above. This
demonstrates engineering decisions and evidence without presenting the demo as an
already production-certified enterprise agent platform.

pages.body:
# Optional GCP judgement gateway

Architecture reading order: [exact agent implementation](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md),
[Terraform/GCP component inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md), then
[enterprise decisions and gaps](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md). This document is the operations
runbook. The gateway evidence below retains its 2026-10-25 verification; native
ADK inference was additionally verified and parked on 2026-10-29. This is not a
fresh status query on each documentation update. "Private" means IAM-authenticated
invocation here; the current service has network-reachable ingress.

The local city works without GCP. The optional switch sends only a bounded retry judgement to a private Cloud Run gateway using Vertex AI. Inventory, fulfillment, dispatch, couriers, movement, custody and SQL policy enforcement remain local and deterministic. This is a hosted judgement role, not a hosted fleet. A live deployment and UI verification were completed on 2026-10-24, followed by verified teardown on 2026-10-25. The project was restored on 2026-10-25 and is parked with billing disabled. The cloud demo is currently off; see [verification](GCP-VERIFICATION.md).

`infra/gcp-ai` is a standalone Terraform root with its own local state. It owns
one persistent, dedicated project, with optional runtime infrastructure. It has no
Scrapmarket dependencies. Never import a shared project or reuse another root's
state. The restored simulation project is imported into its original state.
Project deletion is blocked by both `deletion_policy = "PREVENT"` and
`lifecycle.prevent_destroy`. Keep private variables, plans and state out of Git.

## Daily commands

For native ADK restaurant inference, use `make gcp-vertex-start` followed by
`make demo-adk-vertex`, then `make gcp-stop`. This inference-only path retains a
dedicated `restaurant-adk` service account and enables billing without creating
the gateway or image repository. Only the one-shot local worker receives temporary
impersonated ADC and the ignored Jev credential; the city UI remains offline.
See [restaurant comparison and exact spending limits](ADK-RESTAURANT.md).

From the repository root (Python 3.12+ with only its standard library):

```bash
python3 scripts/gcp_demo.py start
python3 scripts/gcp_demo.py status
python3 scripts/gcp_demo.py stop
```

`make gcp-start`, `make gcp-status` and `make gcp-stop` are equivalent aliases.
The city, homes, stores, stock, orders, queues, roles, memory and rules run locally
in Docker. Building the city and testing deterministic agent/event behavior
requires no GCP deployment or inference. Leave the project parked for that work.

`start` explicitly links billing, creates the image repository, builds/pushes the
small gateway image locally, deploys its immutable digest and reconnects the
local app with a read-only ADC mount. It makes GCP AI available in Configure;
it does not select it or change saved runs. Startup itself makes no model calls.
Image storage and Cloud Run usage can incur charges while enabled. Model charges
begin only when an explicitly cloud-enabled run asks the recovery judge for a
decision. Every stock reservation, route movement and queue event remains local.
Use traces to compare local rules against those selected model decisions.

`stop` resets the app to local mode first, deletes the gateway and stored images
with billing still linked, then unlinks billing. Project, APIs, service accounts,
custom role and free IAM bindings remain. Repeated stop on a parked project does
not relink billing. A deletion failure prevents billing unlinking so cleanup can
be retried. A local app reset failure is reported after attempting cloud cleanup.

`status` reads project lifecycle, billing, actual Cloud Run services, Terraform
runtime resources and local provider availability. With billing enabled it also
lists repositories; otherwise that check is explicitly unavailable. It makes no
model calls and never enables billing to answer a status request. A parked result
is not a billing invoice and does not erase earlier charges.

Prerequisites: gcloud/Terraform/Docker on PATH, Docker running, existing protected
project/IAM state in this root, the ignored `infra/gcp-ai/deploy.auto.tfvars.json`,
and local ADC (`gcloud auth application-default login`). The CLI reads the selected
project/region from that private file. `GCP_ADC_DIRECTORY` can override the usual
local ADC directory; no keys are downloaded. Commands work from any working
directory when invoked with the script's path. Use `APP_PORT` if not 8010.

Commands validate saved plans before applying: foundation changes, replacements,
unexpected resources and another project's runtime are rejected. Desired flags
are saved only after successful apply to the ignored
`zz-demo.auto.tfvars.json`, which overrides the bootstrap values on future plans.
Saved plans remain ignored. Start/stop share a lock; if a process is forcibly
terminated, inspect status and confirm it has stopped before removing
`infra/gcp-ai/.demo-command.lock`. If startup fails after creating resources,
inspect status and run stop. Neither command runs a model evaluation automatically.

## Manual bootstrap (first setup or troubleshooting)

An operator needs project creation and billing-link permissions, Terraform, gcloud and Docker. Select a supported model and Vertex location explicitly; no model or region is assumed. Set `project_id`, `billing_account`, `region`, `vertex_region`, `vertex_model`, and optionally one of `org_id` or `folder_id` in a private tfvars file. Billing, runtime infrastructure and the gateway all default off. Terraform 1.7+ is needed for the mocked lifecycle tests.

1. From `infra/gcp-ai`, run `terraform init`, review `terraform plan`, then `terraform apply`. With all enable flags false this keeps the protected project, six API registrations, both keyless service accounts, the prediction-only custom role and scoped IAM bindings. Set `invoker_members` to explicit operators in the private variables to configure keyless caller impersonation. To bootstrap the repository, set `enable_billing=true`, `enable_runtime=true`, `enable_gateway=false`, review and apply again. This links billing and creates the image repository without Cloud Run; existing identities are reused.
2. From the repository root, build `infra/gcp-ai/Dockerfile` and push the image to the `image_repository` output using an operator's authenticated Docker registry login. For example, `docker build -f infra/gcp-ai/Dockerfile -t REGION-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/judgement/gateway:VERSION .` then `docker push` that same tag. Prefer its immutable digest for `gateway_image`. The image must be this gateway, not an arbitrary server.
3. Set `enable_gateway=true`, `gateway_image` to that image, and `invoker_members` to explicit operator principals such as `user:you@example.com`. Review and apply again. There is no `allUsers` binding. Terraform retains the dedicated keyless caller service account and grants only listed operators permission to mint its tokens.
4. Set the server environment variable `DELIVERY_GCP_AI_ENDPOINT` to the `gateway_url` output and select GCP AI mode in the city configuration. The mode is frozen per session. Local mode remains the default. Changing settings affects new sessions only.

Runtime authentication uses Application Default Credentials and an audience-bound Cloud Run ID token. Run `gcloud auth application-default login` locally, then set `DELIVERY_GCP_AI_CALLER_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` to the `caller_service_account` Terraform output. The adapter uses your ADC to impersonate that account and mint an ID token without a downloaded key. Terraform grants listed operators `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` only on this caller account and grants that account `roles/run.invoker` only on the gateway. On Cloud Run, attached credentials can supply tokens directly when attached to the authorized caller account. Never use service-account key files or API keys. The gateway runtime receives a project-owned custom role containing only `aiplatform.endpoints.predict` in this dedicated project. Both service accounts, the custom role and their identity-level IAM bindings are owned by this root and retained during routine shutdown. The Cloud Run invocation binding belongs to the deleted service and is recreated with it. Operator identities outside the project are not deleted.

## Contract and limits

`CloudJudge(endpoint).review(context, memory, candidate=proposal)` returns `Judgment`: `decision` is exactly `approve_retry` or `deny_retry`, with a short `reason`, configured `model`, and input/output token counts. The caller reserves its durable model budget **before** invoking this adapter, records the decision, and denies on any authentication, transport, validation or budget error. The caller may approve only its already computed candidate; SQL independently checks deadline, retry and custody invariants.

Only numeric allowlisted job facts, numeric candidate summary (`estimated_seconds`, `remaining_seconds`, `route_nodes`) and memory entry count leave the local application. The gateway adds a reviewed, synthetic seven-meal supermarket snapshot as read-only business reference. Full roads, names, basket IDs, courier IDs, arbitrary prompts and memory bodies are excluded. This gateway has no database, queue, browser or arbitrary tool interface. A request is bounded to 8192 serialized bytes, the client waits 30 seconds, Vertex has a 5 second token-count timeout and 15 second generation timeout, output including reported reasoning is limited to 256 tokens, and responses are size/schema checked. Retries are not automatic. Cloud Run scales to zero and at most one instance, with four concurrent requests. These are usage bounds, not a guaranteed monetary cap; model pricing and other project usage can create charges. Choose a model with known price/context limits and use the local durable budget as the admission gate.

## Manual shutdown (the stop command runs these phases)

Routine shutdown uses **apply**, not `terraform destroy`. Keep the project and
its state. In `infra/gcp-ai`, run these two phases in order, reviewing each plan:

```bash
terraform plan -var='enable_billing=true' -var='enable_runtime=false' -var='enable_gateway=false' -out=stop-runtime.tfplan
terraform apply stop-runtime.tfplan
terraform plan -var='enable_billing=false' -var='enable_runtime=false' -var='enable_gateway=false' -out=park.tfplan
terraform apply park.tfplan
```

Phase one deletes Cloud Run (including revisions), its service-specific invocation
binding, and repository/images. The free IAM foundation stays in state: both
service accounts, the prediction-only custom role, its runtime binding, and
operator impersonation permissions on the caller.
Billing must stay linked until deletion finishes: Artifact Registry management
requests can fail with billing disabled. Phase two unlinks billing. For manual operation, save
all three flags as false in the private override so the next ordinary plan stays
parked. The command writes its own `zz-demo.auto.tfvars.json` after successful apply. Clear the obsolete gateway image digest; rebuild and push it
when starting another session. Do not unlink billing first or apply all three
false directly from an active deployment.

API registrations can remain enabled without provisioned runtime resources;
`disable_on_destroy=false` avoids service dependency failures. A parked state
tracks the protected project, six API registrations and five IAM resources (12
resources total). Verify a no-change plan, `ACTIVE` project,
`billingEnabled: false`, and absence of Cloud Run services. Confirm repository
removal during phase one; once billing is disabled its list API may be unavailable.
Recreate the local app with base `compose.yaml` to remove cloud credentials and
endpoint settings. Historical charges and retained platform audit records are
not erased. This switch controls this root's resources, not resources manually
created elsewhere or unrelated projects.

Full project deletion requires a separate explicit decision and deliberate removal
of both protection settings. An ordinary destroy plan must fail on `prevent_destroy`.

[Google restoration and billing behavior](https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/delete-restore-projects)
and [Terraform project deletion protection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/7.14.1/docs/resources/google_project).

## Verification and sources

The adapter tests use mocked transport and never contact GCP. `terraform fmt`, provider initialization and `terraform validate` pass. Live deployment evidence and initial/final eval outcomes are recorded in [verification](GCP-VERIFICATION.md).

Official references: [Cloud Run service identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/service-identity), [authenticated invocation and ID tokens](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service), [Vertex REST generation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/start/quickstart), [Vertex response and token metadata](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/GenerateContentResponse), [Terraform project deletion policy](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/resources/google_project), [Terraform Cloud Run deletion protection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/resources/cloud_run_v2_service).

## Local Docker opt-in

The regular `compose.yaml` never mounts cloud credentials. For the explicit GCP
option, set `DELIVERY_GCP_AI_ENDPOINT`, `DELIVERY_GCP_AI_CALLER_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`,
and `GCP_ADC_DIRECTORY` (the local directory containing the ADC file created by
`gcloud auth application-default login`). Then run
`docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.gcp-ai.yaml up -d --build app`.
The override mounts that directory read-only; never copy ADC into the repository
or image. Select GCP AI recovery judge in Configure and save for the next run.
Each cloud-enabled session freezes its gateway origin. Reverting to local rules
affects new sessions and makes no inference requests. The UI switch does not
apply or destroy Terraform. Use the isolated Terraform root for lifecycle changes.


## Guided redeployment and inspection

Keep the demo local until an explicit cloud session is wanted. Reuse the restored
project ID and original standalone state. The original service accounts and custom
role were recovered and imported on 2026-10-25; their unique IDs are unchanged.
Routine shutdown now retains these identities, so no repeated recovery is needed.
Enable billing and runtime first with the gateway off, rebuild/push the deleted
image, then enable the gateway with a new
immutable digest. Follow the bootstrap steps above and refresh the local compose
override with the new endpoint. Never reuse Scrapmarket state.

For the next guided session, inspect these in order:

1. **Ownership:** review the Terraform plan, dedicated project, billing link and all
   resources. Confirm no shared-project changes or public invocation binding.
2. **Identity:** inspect the runtime prediction-only role, caller's service-specific
   invocation permission, and keyless authentication. Confirm anonymous requests fail.
3. **Data boundary:** inspect the seven-meal synthetic snapshot and actual serialized
   request. Confirm names, customer details and private memory bodies stay local.
4. **Agent boundary:** follow a stock reservation through queued fulfillment and
   dispatch. Inspect role-scoped tools, memory and SQL enforcement.
5. **Model and cost:** inspect the configured model, scale limits, per-run call/token
   reservations and returned usage. Explain why those controls are not a dollar cap.
6. **Evals:** run the fixed recovery cases, distinguish policy-gate answers from actual
   model answers, and compare with the preserved initial failure and guarded results.
7. **Recorded live switch:** inspect the [paired cloud/local evidence](GCP-VERIFICATION.md)
   for stock, custody and retry invariants. The former grid-UI verification script
   was retired with the Delivery workspace; this receipt is historical evidence.
8. **Cleanup:** delete runtime resources with billing linked, then unlink billing.
   Verify the protected project remains active and state retains project/APIs/IAM,
   and billing is disabled. Recreate the app using base compose.

Retain sanitized receipts and commit verified changes. Keep credentials, Terraform
state, private variables and saved plans out of Git.


## Recovered IAM evidence

The original caller (`108780209802092054377`) and runtime
(`105662098881414929441`) were undeleted by numeric ID, and
`boundedJudgePredict` was undeleted and imported. It still grants only
`aiplatform.endpoints.predict`. Recovery creates no service-account keys.
See [IAM recovery receipt](evidence/gcp-iam-recovered.json).
Google documents that [undeleting preserves the original identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-accounts-delete-undelete).

# GCP deployment verification — 2026-10-24

## Deployment and data boundary

A new dedicated project, `mds-ai-judge-261024-c7b4`, was provisioned from
`infra/gcp-ai` using the operator-selected billing account. No Scrapmarket project,
Terraform state or resources were modified. Cloud Run is in `europe-west1`;
Vertex uses the explicitly selected `global` endpoint. This is not an EU-only
inference residency claim. Only synthetic data was sent.

Ready revision: `judgement-00002-92k`. Immutable image:
`sha256:71834c8a002596752dd560c957ae75dae86041c582467805b6f3473292bbdd15`.
Model: `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, minimal thinking. Prompt version:
`recovery-v2-seven-meals`. Snapshot SHA-256:
`5be219156af219ac97f41dd53e96024107e5eb68457da14cd3015c1c8d914f19`.
The snapshot contains seven meals, 17 ingredients and three fictional supermarkets.
It is reviewed read-only context; the judge does not perform procurement.

## Eval findings and repair

The initial live run passed 4/6 cases: five valid model responses, one provider
error, and one unsafe model approval when required facts were missing. The SQL
executor already retained independent policy enforcement. We preserved this result
rather than treating deployment success as model correctness.

We added a deterministic gateway preflight for missing facts, absent candidates,
retry exhaustion, deadline and route-cost constraints. Final system results:
6/6 cases passed, zero provider errors and zero hard-policy violations. This was
**one model decision and five policy-gate denials**, not six LLM decisions.
Six toy cases do not establish general model quality, a production SLO, or business
uplift over rules. See the [initial](evidence/gcp-judge-initial.json) and
[guarded](evidence/gcp-judge-guarded.json) receipts.

The guarded eval used 2,150 input and 35 output tokens. At the documented global
rates of $0.30 / $2.50 per million input/output tokens, its successful model usage
is estimated at $0.0007325. This excludes failed/unreported generations, earlier
probes, Cloud Run, storage, logging, taxes and currency conversion. It is not an
invoice or project-wide cost cap. [Google pricing](https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing).

## End-to-end UI switch

The former live-cloud script (retired with the Delivery grid UI) configured
seed 71, 15 minutes of demand, four orders/hour, traffic 1, dropout intensity 0.4,
and three couriers based at one shop. The seed naturally withdraws bike-1 at
simulated second 694; no incident was injected after session creation.

The GCP-mode run `fe8fbad6-103f-42ff-8fd1-1e12e384cb02` recorded one actual model
approval, one durable 8,448-token reservation and no fallback. The paired local-mode
run `95057578-594a-42ed-b2e1-2862104f139e` recorded zero model calls. All stock,
assignment, custody, retry-approval and budget invariants passed; browser errors
were empty. [UI verification receipt](evidence/gcp-switch-verification.json).

Unauthenticated invocation returned 403; authenticated malformed input returned
422. Neither negative check invokes the model. The caller can invoke only this
service; the runtime custom role contains only `aiplatform.endpoints.predict`.
No service-account keys were created. [Negative checks](evidence/gcp-negative-checks.json).

## Teardown coverage

A reviewed `terraform plan -destroy` contains exactly 15 deletions, covering the
service and revisions, invocation IAM, custom role and prediction binding, both
service accounts, repository/images, enabled-service resources, and the dedicated
project. Every planned resource belongs to this project. Project deletion owns
implicit service agents and other platform-created project children. No shared
billing account or operator identity is deleted.

**Teardown executed on 2026-10-25:** Terraform reported 15 destroyed resources;
`terraform state list` is empty. Google reports the dedicated project as
`DELETE_REQUESTED`, so final project erasure remains asynchronous and subject to
platform retention. The local app is healthy with `local: true`, `gcp_ai: false`
and the cloud credential override removed. Scrapmarket was not touched.
[Actual teardown receipt](evidence/gcp-teardown-result.json).
The earlier [plan receipt](evidence/gcp-teardown-plan.json) records the pre-execution check.

## Enterprise interpretation

The useful interview evidence is controlled rollout and a documented failure/repair,
not a claim that an LLM is necessary for numeric feasibility. Keep local rules as the
baseline and default. Before exposing more users, add gateway-wide admission budgets,
held-out business evals, stronger release automation, recovery SLOs and finance
reconciliation. [Architecture and tradeoffs](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md).


## Restored persistent project (2026-10-25)

After the completed historical teardown above, the user requested keeping the
project between demos. The dedicated project was restored, imported into the
same Terraform root, and protected against deletion. Its current lifecycle is
`ACTIVE`, billing is disabled, and state contains only `google_project.ai`.
The live parked plan is unchanged; Cloud Run lists zero services. Artifact
Registry listing is blocked by `BILLING_DISABLED`; its repository was confirmed
deleted during the earlier teardown, rather than inferred absent from that error.
An initial attempt to register APIs immediately after restoration encountered
service propagation errors; parked mode does not need those registrations.

Six mocked Terraform runs cover parked defaults, active deployment, deleting
runtime while retaining billing, final parked mode, and rejection of invalid
runtime/gateway combinations. These are plan/apply tests with a mocked provider,
not a second paid deployment. A live full destroy plan was rejected by
`lifecycle.prevent_destroy`. Follow the two-phase shutdown in GCP-AI.md, not the
historical full-delete procedure above.
[Restoration receipt](evidence/gcp-project-restored.json).


## Persistent free IAM recovery (2026-10-25)

Both original service accounts were undeleted using the numeric IDs from the
original teardown plan, then imported at their indexed Terraform addresses.
`boundedJudgePredict` was undeleted and imported with the original single
prediction permission. Free API registrations and narrow IAM bindings are now
retained between sessions. The parked state holds 12 foundation resources:
project, six API registrations, two accounts, custom role and two bindings.
Billing remains disabled and Cloud Run has no services. Artifact Registry's
listing API still requires billing; prior successful repository deletion and
its absence from current state are the available repository evidence.

Seven mocked lifecycle runs now apply active, runtime-off and billing-off states,
then plan restart with the same service-account unique IDs. No paid runtime was
redeployed for this check. A live parked plan must have zero changes.
The earlier project-only receipt remains a historical checkpoint.
[Current IAM recovery receipt](evidence/gcp-iam-recovered.json).


## One-command demo lifecycle (2026-10-25)

`python scripts/gcp_demo.py start` was exercised against the isolated project:
billing linked, the repository was created, a local build was pushed and pinned
by digest, the private gateway deployed, and the local app exposed GCP judge mode.
Read-only status confirmed one service/repository and all 12 foundation resources.
No simulation or model inference was started by lifecycle verification.

`python scripts/gcp_demo.py stop` reset the app to local-only, successfully deleted
the service/repository before unlinking billing, and preserved the free foundation.
Final status: ACTIVE project, billing disabled, no service/runtime resources,
local-only app, and unchanged original caller/runtime numeric IDs. A refreshed
Terraform plan had zero changes. The repository list is unavailable after billing
unlink; deletion was observed during the successful first cleanup phase.

Twenty offline command regression tests cover plan rejection for foundation or
cross-project changes, shutdown sequencing and failures, credential isolation,
idempotence and locking. These complement the live lifecycle check.
[Command verification receipt](evidence/gcp-demo-commands.json).


The first broad container run exposed a copied Windows pytest assertion cache:
153 passed and the existing lease-wait test failed. Running that test directly
from source passed. Docker context now excludes nested `__pycache__`/bytecode;
the rebuilt Linux image passed all **155 tests**. Ruff and source type checks
also pass. This build reproducibility fix is committed separately from the CLI.

# Queue and agent tracing

OpenTelemetry follows a message from publication through the worker, fixed tools,
inference preparation, database effects and downstream publications. Tracing is
disabled by default. It does not enable model calls or alter model budgets.

The [observability architecture](ARCHITECTURE-OBSERVABILITY.md) describes the
order lifecycle, native Cloud Trace exporter and optional streaming analytics.
The Jaeger and Google collector profiles below remain supported. Use one export
configuration per process; the legacy collector selector takes precedence when set.

## Free local Jaeger

```bash
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.tracing.yaml up -d --build --wait
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.tracing.yaml exec -T app delivery init
```

Run a simulation or restaurant scenario, then open `/agent-traces` in the app.
The recent trace table links 32-character OTel IDs to
[Jaeger](http://localhost:16686). The collector uses transient memory; restarting
it clears its traces. PostgreSQL evidence remains. Only Jaeger's UI is exposed,
bound to loopback; OTLP ingestion stays on the Compose network.

For local Python processes, use `DELIVERY_OTEL_EXPORTER=jaeger` and an OTLP HTTP
endpoint at `http://localhost:4318/v1/traces` on a separately running Jaeger.
The Compose collector intentionally does not publish its ingestion port.

## Optional Google Cloud Trace

The application exports OTLP to the Google-built collector, which authenticates
with ADC and sends traces to the Google Telemetry API. No cloud trace exporter
starts unless both the `gcp` mode and explicit opt-in flag are configured.

The exporting identity needs `roles/telemetry.tracesWriter` on the destination
project and `roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer` on its ADC quota project.
Enable the Telemetry and Cloud Trace APIs if organization policy disabled them.
Use a dedicated runtime service account on GCP; no service-account key is needed.
`infra/gcp-ai/telemetry.tf` provisions those APIs and a trace-only exporter identity
when `enable_telemetry=true`; it defaults to false and deploys no collector.
The `telemetry_service_account` output identifies the service account. Use it as
the GCP collector runtime identity, or obtain impersonated ADC for an authorized
local principal listed in `invoker_members`:

```bash
gcloud auth application-default login --impersonate-service-account=TRACE_EXPORTER_EMAIL
```

```bash
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=your-project
export GCP_ADC_DIRECTORY="$HOME/.config/gcloud"
export DELIVERY_OTEL_CLOUD_ENABLED=1
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.tracing-gcp.yaml up -d --build --wait
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.tracing-gcp.yaml exec -T app delivery init
```

This is an explicit cloud export operation and may incur observability charges.
It is separate from the inference cost ledger in `cloud_ai.py`. Cloud tracing
defaults to a 10% root trace sample rate; local Jaeger records all traces.
`DELIVERY_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO` accepts values from 0 to 1. Parent sampling decisions
carry across the queue. A trace link may point to a sampled-out or expired trace.

For a GCP-hosted application, use `config/otel-collector-gcp.yaml` in a collector
sidecar and set the application's `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` to
`http://localhost:4318/v1/traces`. The runtime identity supplies ADC. The supplied
Compose cloud override is a local opt-in demonstration, not a deployed service.

## Evidence and boundaries

- `events.trace_id` remains the business correlation ID. Migration 026 introduced
  the separate W3C envelope; migration 027 reconciles both branch histories and
  adds lease-fenced context updates. Each run and canonical order key has one
  trace ID. SQL-produced descendants inherit the parent without payload changes.
- Retries retain the incoming trace context and record a new attempt span. Queue
  failures produce error status without persisting exception messages to traces.
- Decision receipts include `detail.telemetry.trace_id` and `span_id` while a
  valid span exists. `/api/telemetry/traces` returns up to 30 recent event traces.
- Spans contain run/event IDs, topic, tool or agent name, attempt and error type.
  Model spans also include measured token counts and estimated cost when known.
  They exclude prompts, model responses, event bodies, SQL, secrets and exception
  strings. A dedicated provider avoids automatically exporting third-party ADK
  spans that may contain model input or output.
- Export uses a bounded 2,048-span queue, batches of 256, a five-second timeout,
  and limited attributes. Collector outages can drop spans; PostgreSQL remains
  the authoritative transaction and audit record. Graceful process exit flushes
  the provider; abrupt crash injection can lose its final spans.

## Verification

Inspect the [tracer and privacy limits](../src/delivery/telemetry.py),
[original context migration](../sql/migrations/026_telemetry_context.sql),
[unified context migration](../sql/migrations/027_unified_order_telemetry.sql),
[trace API](../src/delivery/telemetry_api.py),
[Jaeger override](../compose.tracing.yaml),
[cloud override](../compose.tracing-gcp.yaml),
[collector configuration](../config/otel-collector-gcp.yaml), and
[trace-only Terraform identity](../infra/gcp-ai/telemetry.tf).
The [propagation tests](../tests/test_telemetry.py) and
[mocked infrastructure checks](../infra/gcp-ai/tests/telemetry.tftest.hcl)
are available in the documentation source reader.

```bash
docker compose run --rm --no-deps app pytest -q tests/test_telemetry.py
```

Tests use the SDK's in-memory exporter. They verify disabled/cloud opt-in behavior,
context propagation through publication and consumption, retry continuity, safe
links and redaction. They never contact a collector or paid service.

API and collector configuration were checked against current first-party docs:
[Cloud Trace Python instrumentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/setup/python-ot),
[Google-built collector on Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/instrumentation/opentelemetry-collector-cloud-run),
and [Jaeger 2.22](https://www.jaegertracing.io/docs/2.22/getting-started/).

# Run evidence in BigQuery

The simulation stays local. Analytics is an explicit export of existing evidence: it never starts a run, asks a model a question, changes inference admission limits, or executes a BigQuery query. The default workflow writes inspectable local files and needs no Google credentials. Terraform defaults to `enable_bigquery=false` and creates no analytics storage or service account.

## Prepare and inspect a free bundle

From an installed development environment, use an existing offline receipt:

```bash
python3 scripts/export_bigquery.py prepare \
  --receipt artifacts/adk-restaurants-demo.json \
  --output artifacts/bigquery/demo
```

The exporter accepts both native receipt formats:

- Baseline simulation: `artifacts/run-<run-id>.json`, with a nested `run` object containing `id`, timezone-qualified `created_at`, `status`, and model accounting, plus top-level `metrics`. Delivery measurements include orders, delivered/on-time counts, on-time percentage, active/unserved work, delivery cost and cost per delivery.
- ADK comparisons: a top-level timezone-qualified `created_at`, a `profiles` or `arms` list, and per-run `run` UUID, `metrics`, and boolean `invariants` or `outcome_checks`. This includes `artifacts/adk-route-comparison.json` and `artifacts/adk-live-comparison.json`. Generate a fresh offline receipt with `make demo-adk` if needed.

Use either format with the same `prepare --receipt ... --output ...` command. Missing invariant or replay evidence stays unmeasured.

The output contains:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `run_receipts.ndjson` | Run ID, receipt/source hashes, run and export timestamps, profile/scenario/variant, recorded status, replay result, passed/total checks, and cost evidence. |
| `run_kpis.ndjson` | Allowlisted numeric delivery, queue, ADK, search, and router measurements, one row per metric. |
| `manifest.json` | SHA-256, row count and byte count for both tables. |

Raw prompts, transcripts, provider responses, configuration, credentials, and free-form error text are excluded. Unknown metrics remain absent; incomplete cost accounting remains null. `usage_cost_usd` uses known usage at the receipt's frozen tariffs only when every call is accounted for. It is not a billing invoice. `reserved_cost_usd` remains a separate admission amount; explicit zero-paid-call receipts can report zero cost. A missing status is `recorded`, never inferred to be completed.

Baseline `llm_cost_usd`, `llm_calls`, tokens and reservations are retained as numeric KPIs. Their aggregate values do not prove every admitted model call returned usage. Consequently, a baseline receipt with model calls retains null `usage_cost_usd` even if its observed cost is zero. Only an explicit zero call count proves zero model usage for that format; missing call counts do not. The reserved amount remains separately visible.

Preparation refuses to overwrite a bundle. Keep the bundle unchanged for retries. Source files are capped at 32 MiB; each export is capped at 100 runs and 1 MiB. All generated files belong under ignored `artifacts/`.

## Optional cloud setup

This is a separate, opt-in demo alongside the existing GCP judge lifecycle. No cloud deployment or upload runs in CI. Use the dedicated project already configured in the ignored Terraform variables, and review the plan before applying:

```bash
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai plan \
  -var=enable_bigquery=true -var=enable_billing=true \
  -out=analytics-enable.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai apply analytics-enable.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai output bigquery_analytics
```

The plan provisions an EU dataset by default, two tables partitioned by `exported_at` and clustered by run/hash, and the `run_dashboard` GoogleSQL view. Both tables require a partition filter and expire partitions after seven days. Change `bigquery_location` before creating the dataset if required; it is independent of the Vertex region. Retention and the upload size cap bound this demonstration's data footprint; they are not a total billing cap. Storage and dashboard queries can incur charges while enabled.

The keyless `delivery-analytics` service account has a custom dataset-scoped role limited to table create/get/update/updateData and a project role containing only jobs.create. It cannot read table data, delete tables, administer IAM, or invoke Vertex. The uploader sets `CREATE_NEVER`: table creation belongs to Terraform. Only the explicit `invoker_members` can impersonate this identity. No service-account keys are created. Keep dashboard reader access separate from this write-only loader.

## Upload only the reviewed bundle

Use an installed Python environment with the project dependencies and Application Default Credentials. Set the project ID from the Terraform output; no project ID or credentials are committed:

```bash
export ANALYTICS_PROJECT='your-dedicated-project'
export DELIVERY_BIGQUERY_ENABLED=1
python3 scripts/export_bigquery.py upload \
  --bundle artifacts/bigquery/demo \
  --project "$ANALYTICS_PROJECT" \
  --service-account "delivery-analytics@$ANALYTICS_PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --dataset delivery_analytics --location EU \
  --confirm-upload
unset DELIVERY_BIGQUERY_ENABLED
```

Both the environment opt-in and `--confirm-upload` are required before credentials are loaded. The bundle is checked against its manifest before either table is uploaded. Loads append to existing tables, reject unknown columns/bad records, and use stable job IDs derived from the exact destination and frozen bytes. Retrying the same bundle recovers an existing load job after a conflict. The two table loads are independent: after a partial failure, repeat the same upload command. Do not prepare another bundle as a retry. BigQuery job deduplication is bounded by its retained job history; the dashboard additionally selects the latest export per run and collapses duplicate metric rows. Old exports expire with their partitions.

## Looker Studio dashboard

Connect Looker Studio's BigQuery connector to the Terraform output `dashboard_view` using a separate reader identity with the necessary dataset read and project job permissions. The view is ready to select as a table, so no custom SQL is needed in Looker Studio.

Suggested controls are `run_date`, `profile`, `scenario`, and `variant`. Add delivery rate, queue events, dead letters, replay result, and evaluation pass rate; compare measured usage cost with reserved cost in separate series. `evaluation_pass_rate` is the run receipt's boolean-check pass rate, not the entire repository's scenario evaluation score. Missing denominators and missing usage stay null. Both source tables are filtered to the last seven export days. Choose bounded refresh intervals and inspect BigQuery billing before making a dashboard public; this feature does not publish one automatically.

The same view supports baseline receipts: `delivery_rate` divides delivered orders by ADK `scheduled_calls` when present, otherwise baseline `orders`. It also exposes baseline `on_time`, `on_time_pct`, `delivery_cost_eur`, `cost_per_delivery_eur`, `active`, `unserved`, `pending`, and `overdue` columns. `delivery_rate` is a fraction (0–1); the simulator's `on_time_pct` is already a percentage (0–100). A zero denominator remains null, and baseline receipts without outcome checks retain a null evaluation pass rate.

## Park analytics

Stop uploads by clearing `DELIVERY_BIGQUERY_ENABLED`. To return to no analytics storage, explicitly remove this disposable dataset while billing is still linked:

`gcp_demo.py status` lists `analytics_in_state` and `telemetry_in_state`; retained optional components are never reported as fully parked. `stop` checks these resources before restarting the app or changing cloud resources and gives cleanup instructions if any remain. Once cleanup is complete, its parking plans explicitly keep both optional flags false so stale opt-in settings cannot recreate them.

```bash
unset DELIVERY_BIGQUERY_ENABLED
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai plan \
  -var=enable_bigquery=false -var=enable_billing=true \
  -out=analytics-disable.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai apply analytics-disable.tfplan
python3 scripts/gcp_demo.py stop
```

Review the removal plan: it deletes the analytics tables and view. Original local receipts remain available. The dataset refuses to delete unexpected, unmanaged contents. Preserve `enable_bigquery=true` on intervening Terraform commands while the analytics demo is active; command-line flags are not persisted. Remove analytics explicitly before the existing judge stop command unlinks billing. The enabled BigQuery API registration can remain after storage and IAM are removed and does not itself store run data.

## Verification and API references

`tests/test_bigquery_export.py` covers local-only preparation, allowlisting, incomplete accounting, strict opt-in, artifact tampering, stable load IDs, SDK load configuration and recovery, and payload limits. `infra/gcp-ai/tests/bigquery.tftest.hcl` uses the mocked Google provider to check parked defaults, billing opt-in, retention, scoped permissions and the view. These checks make no paid calls. The cloud path has not been live-uploaded as part of this change.

Inspect the [exporter](../src/delivery/bigquery_export.py), [command](../scripts/export_bigquery.py), [unit tests](../tests/test_bigquery_export.py), [Terraform resources](../infra/gcp-ai/bigquery.tf), [infrastructure tests](../infra/gcp-ai/tests/bigquery.tftest.hcl), and [dashboard SQL view](../infra/gcp-ai/sql/run_dashboard.sql).

Official documentation checked on 2026-10-29:

- [Import a local file](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/samples/bigquery-load-from-file) and [Python Client 3.46.2](https://docs.cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/bigquery/latest/google.cloud.bigquery.client.Client): binary file loads, fixed job IDs, location, and job completion.
- [Batch-loading permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/batch-loading-data): table load permissions and jobs.create.
- [BigQuery IAM](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control): resource-scoped grants and separation of data access from job execution.
