# Agent evaluation workflow

Start the local stack (`make up`), then use Bash:

```bash
make eval-agents
```

The disposable checker runs the fixed battery **twice**, writes
`artifacts/health/latest-scenarios.json`, and exits nonzero for a failed or missing
case, changed source, or different repeated outcomes. `make health` includes this
command's evaluator alongside the complete test suite and static checks. Neither
command restarts the running app, Postgres or Redis. Open
[Health & evals → Agent evals](http://localhost:8010/health) to inspect the results.
Refreshing the page only reads receipts; it cannot execute a command.

All worlds use seed **731**, the committed synthetic catalogues/recipes and the
existing 32×32 city. They run in the dedicated **local `delivery_test` database**;
production database names, remote hosts and connection-string overrides are
rejected before creating a world. Model inference is disabled and ingredient
search uses its local adapter. There is no cloud endpoint option. The optional
GCP demo remains independent.

## Cases and scoring

The versioned contract is `data/evals/agent-scenarios.json`. Twelve scenarios
declare 49 criteria, each with a human-readable label and an exact typed expected
value. Booleans and integer counts are different measurements.

| Role | Scenario | Required behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inventory | Two baskets, one unit | One reservation, one safe rejection; scoped stock visibility |
| Inventory | Delayed replenishment | Forecast units remain unavailable until actual receipt |
| Inventory | Crash before acknowledgement | Actual worker-process crash rolls back; lease retry has one effect |
| Restaurant | Available pantry | Deliver pizza without unnecessary sourcing |
| Restaurant | Market forwarding | Empty nearest market forwards flour request; ingredients arrive before cooking |
| Restaurant | Replacement declined | Record refusal and reject without cooking or consuming ingredients |
| Restaurant | Replacement approved | Household consent and kitchen approval both precede cooking |
| Dispatcher | Assignment race | Two workers contend for one courier; one job assigned, one deferred |
| Dispatcher | Traffic and retry | Congestion affects ETAs; retry needs approval; infeasible job is abandoned |
| Courier | Assignment authority | Other courier cannot read/accept brief or recall memory; motion waits for ACK |
| Courier | Dropout handoff | Replacement gets recorded parcel checkpoint, prior courier and source events |
| Courier | Physical arrival | Completion follows world arrival; route ETA equals edge duration sum |

A case passes only when **every declared criterion** passes and execution/cleanup
succeeds. A safe business rejection is a successful evaluation when rejection is
the specified outcome. Case and role scores are passed criteria divided by their
declared criteria; missing measurements receive no credit. The dashboard always
shows case failure counts alongside scores. Missing receipts have no score;
partial receipts cannot become a complete pass.

Scores are recomputed by the reader from the committed contract and measured
values. A receipt cannot supply its own expected values, headline pass count or
score. Unknown/duplicate cases, extra fields, malformed types, missing configuration
hashes, incorrect repeat hashes and mismatched manifest versions are rejected.

## What actually runs

`delivery.scenario_evals` creates eight small isolated fixture worlds. Agents are
the existing `LocalAgent` workers with their real per-run/store/role Postgres
logins, permissions, tool budgets, typed memory and durable queue leases. The
controller sets up stock, injects disruptions, advances virtual time and observes
results as a trusted operator. Agents communicate through queued events; the
evaluator does not replace their decisions with an oracle. Dispatcher contention
uses two concurrent workers, and inventory recovery kills a real subprocess.

The controller retires short-lived database identities and deletes its worlds in
`finally`, including after a fixture error. Failure receipts store fixed error
codes, never exception messages, SQL strings, connection URLs, event payloads or
memory bodies. The retained event trail contains only fixture-relative sequence,
topic, trace, queue state, attempts and scheduled simulation seconds. Fixture
sequence numbers are local to the receipt; deleted database events cannot be
opened later. Supply replay is checked before cleanup.

Two evaluations cannot interleave through the CLI: it holds a Postgres advisory
lock. Existing simulation runs in the application's `delivery` database are
unaffected. The test suite verifies that the battery leaves the pre-existing
test-run IDs and role identities unchanged, and that an injected fixture error
still cleans up without exposing its exception text.

## Reproducibility and limits

Receipts retain manifest version/hash, seed, effective configuration hashes, source
fingerprint, UTC creation time and a business-outcome hash for **each** repetition.
The hash includes typed observations and fixed error codes. It excludes wall time,
random run IDs, global SQL event IDs, and which racing worker wins: both possible
winners are valid, but one courier must still receive exactly one job.

Each repetition's observations are preserved and checked against its hash. A later
passing repeat cannot erase an earlier failed case. Each criterion keeps its first
explicit failure across repeats, otherwise its first missing measurement, otherwise
the final passing value. Criteria and event trails identify their repetition. An
omission cannot hide a measured failure from another repeat. Input hash drift also
produces a failed receipt, including when one setup attempt fails before creating
the world. A mismatch fails reproducibility even if both individual outcomes
otherwise meet the criteria. Starting the checker replaces any previous green
receipt with unmeasured evidence until the new battery finishes.

For a quicker diagnostic run after building the image:

```bash
docker compose run --rm --no-deps app python3 scripts/eval_agents.py --reproduce 1
```

The page labels a single run as repeatability **not measured**. Results from changed
sources or older than 24 hours remain historical. Rebuild the running app after
source changes so its fingerprint can match the checker. These are local receipts,
not signed attestations against a hostile host operator.

This is a fixed **development regression battery for rules-based agents**. It
measures coordinated business and permission behavior, not LLM reasoning quality,
production latency, cost per model decision, held-out generalization, or superiority
of one architecture/memory strategy. Those remain separate unmeasured benchmarks.

## Google-native model evaluation

[Committed-snapshot verification](evidence/google-native-evals.json) records the
test counts, scripted-arm metrics and limits of the latest local evaluation.

The native files are `evals/adk/restaurant.evalset.json` and
`evals/adk/customer_service.test.json`, with ten cases each. Install the pinned
runtime from `requirements.lock` (including `google-adk[eval]`), then run from the
repository root in Bash:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.lock
python3 -m pip install --no-deps -e .
adk eval evals/adk/restaurant evals/adk/restaurant.evalset.json \
  --config_file_path evals/adk/test_config.json
adk eval evals/adk/customer_service evals/adk/customer_service.test.json \
  --config_file_path evals/adk/test_config.json
python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_adk_evalsets.py
python3 scripts/eval_agents.py --suite adk --repeat 3
```

`AgentEvaluator` and the CLI use the same EvalSet schema and deterministic
trajectory/response-match metrics. Both agents use `adk_offline.py`, with no
provider fallback. Tests deny provider initialization and HTTP; the CLI child also
denies sockets. Restaurant tools use in-memory fixtures and the production plan
schema. Actual SQL scope, admission, durability and migration-019 trace ingestion
remain covered by integration tests. Scripted classification is not evidence of
language understanding.

The repeated-arm receipt is `artifacts/evals/candidate.json`. `--repeat k`
(1–100) applies only to model arms, with a fresh session per attempt.
`--reproduce 1|2|3` independently controls SQL repeatability; `--suite all` runs
both. The default suite remains `scenarios` for compatibility with `make health`.
A container without Git can receive `DELIVERY_SOURCE_REVISION`; otherwise the
receipt is labelled unversioned. `make eval-adk` runs the model suite in Docker.

## Error analysis and categories

1. Start with the failing case, arm, repetition and category; reproduce locally.
2. Inspect the request's declared functions and the response's actual calls.
   Requests contain repeated history: count only new response calls.
3. Compare arguments and ordered steps against a reviewed reference. A correct
   final reply does not excuse an invented tool or a wrong supplier.
4. Check recovery evidence. A successful corrected tool response counts; an
   attempted retry without a response does not. Durable tool receipts capture
   terminal results when summarization is skipped.
5. Promote a minimal regression, rerun code checks, native evals and the original
   SQL integration test, then refine policy or prompts.

`delivery.trajectory_evals.read_trace(url, event_id)` reads one event from
`restaurant_model_calls` and `restaurant_tool_receipts` using an operator
connection. Migration 019 added request/response/latency columns; no new migration
or agent table grant is needed. `score_trajectory` reports multiset tool
precision/recall, exact-argument precision/recall, field differences, ordered LCS
match, extra/missing steps, model/tool step counts, incomplete dispatches and
recovery rate. No observed errors means recovery is null, not perfect.

The health taxonomy explicitly includes **schema**, **length** and
**invented_tool**. Schema checks reject malformed replies and unexpected
arguments. Length checks enforce the 1–500 character summary/reply boundaries.
Invented-tool checks use the declared capability set and never alias misspelled
names. These checks run before any semantic judge and spend no judge quota. Task
and trajectory correctness are separate gate categories.

## Promote stored evidence

Write an explicit reference containing tool names and arguments. Never treat a
failed output as its own desired answer. For example, using Bash:

```bash
mkdir -p artifacts/evals
cat > artifacts/evals/reference.json <<'JSON'
[{"name":"finish_decision","args":{"summary":"Compared the quotes."}}]
JSON
python3 scripts/promote_trace.py \
  --receipt artifacts/adk-route-comparison.json \
  --pointer /arms/3/evidence --event-id 123 \
  --reference artifacts/evals/reference.json \
  --id reviewed-cost-finish --description 'Reviewed terminal-tool regression' \
  --expect-category invented_tool
```

Replace 123 with the actual event and provide its complete reference. Alternatively
use `--stored-trace --event-id 123` with operator `DATABASE_URL` supplied through
the environment. Multi-event receipts require an event selector. Each promotion
creates the next `data/evals/golden/vN/` directory without overwriting prior
versions; the latest version of each case ID is evaluated. Review the diff before
committing. Reference arguments and descriptions still need privacy review. Raw
prompts, model thoughts and tool-result bodies are omitted; capability arguments
and minimal success/error classifications survive.

Golden case **001-cost-invented-finish** preserves a terminal-call excerpt from
the historical cost-mode receipt: `finish_finish_decision` instead of
`finish_decision`. Its expected result is an invented-tool rejection and zero
name recall. A passing negative regression means the scorer caught the known
failure, not that the historical run succeeded. The native `cost-source` case
separately verifies the current scripted agent's complete correct trajectory.

## Reliability, cost and latency

Every attempt is retained, including failures. **pass^k** is the empirical fraction
of distinct cases passing **all k** attempts. It is neither pass@k (at least one
success) nor the pooled pass rate raised to a power. Missing, duplicate or
unbalanced repetitions invalidate comparisons.

Seeded percentile bootstrap 95% intervals resample cases, keeping whole repeat
groups. Repeats are not extra independent cases. A one-case sample has no interval.
At all-pass/all-fail boundaries bootstrap intervals are degenerate; this does not
establish certainty about unseen tasks. Fixed development cases are not a random
production sample. Scripted pass^k/timings measure fixture stability, not live-model
reliability or production performance.

Cost per successful task divides the cost of all attempts, including failures,
by successful attempts. Unknown usage never becomes free; reservations provide a
separate conservative figure. Zero successes yield null. P95 latency includes
failures and uses an interpolated percentile. The recovery-judge script reports
these metrics too. Comparisons show main/candidate values and deltas; wall-clock
timing remains diagnostic because shared CI runners are noisy.

## PR gate and main baseline

The `evals` job runs on pull requests and main pushes without cloud credentials or
paid calls. Code checks precede native evals and three fresh scripted attempts per
case. Successful main runs store `eval-baseline-v1` for 90 days, including reviewed
`config/eval-gate.json` thresholds and source revision. PRs download the artifact
from the successful main run for their exact base SHA. PR changes cannot select
an alternate baseline or quietly weaken its stored thresholds.

CI collects model attempts with `--record-only`: quality mismatches stay in the
receipt for the statistical comparison instead of failing the collection step.
Runner exceptions, incomplete or duplicate repeats, inconsistent pass/category
values, and missing or failed golden regressions still fail immediately. The
ordinary CLI retains its nonzero exit for any failed attempt. Native ADK tests
copy applications into writable temporary directories, so the CLI can save its
`.adk` history even when container source files are read-only. Both CI jobs
explicitly disable telemetry and BigQuery export.

No baseline exists before the workflow first lands: that bootstrap run is explicitly
`baseline_missing`, with no quality comparison claim. Missing or expired artifacts
have the same status. Obtain a successful main run before relying on comparisons.

Comparisons require identical fixture hashes, modes, repeat counts, arms and case
IDs. Changed cohorts or corrupt receipts fail validation, not a statistical quality
test. Reference changes require a reviewed main baseline refresh. Saved headline
scores are ignored and recomputed from rows.

A quality regression requires all three:

- At least eight distinct paired cases.
- The lower end of the case-bootstrap 95% pass-rate-drop interval exceeds the
  permitted drop: zero for schema/length/invented tools, 0.05 for task/trajectory.
- An exact one-sided paired sign test passes family-wise 0.05, Bonferroni-adjusted
  across every arm and category.

A single fluctuation does not fail the statistical gate. Deterministic contract
failures and invalid artifacts still fail verification. Cost/latency deltas do not
fail the quality gate. One red/green PR comment is updated with evidence. A green
bootstrap or insufficient-evidence label is not proof of equivalence. Forks whose
tokens cannot comment retain Markdown as a job summary/artifact. The workflow
does not execute candidate code through `pull_request_target`.

```bash
python3 scripts/eval_gate.py --candidate artifacts/evals/candidate.json \
  --baseline artifacts/evals/main/candidate.json \
  --baseline-revision MAIN_COMMIT_SHA \
  --thresholds artifacts/evals/main/eval-gate.json
```

## Optional manual Vertex judge

`vertex-eval.yml` is `workflow_dispatch` only, main only, with an explicit `paid`
input. Configure the `vertex-evals` environment variables `GCP_EVAL_PROJECT`,
`GCP_EVAL_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` and `GCP_EVAL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` with an identity
authorized for Vertex evaluation. It judges existing synthetic customer replies
from `data/evals/customer-replies.json`, without generating candidates.

`cloud_ai.py` sends the documented `evaluateInstances` pointwise request with
`gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, one sample, no thinking, at most 256 output tokens, an
8 KiB request and a 30-second timeout. It bypasses the SDK's internally retrying
batch helper. No model fallback is allowed. A SQLite ledger reserves USD 0.01
before each request, enforcing USD 0.05 per run; even if twelve calls are
requested, money admits at most five. Reservations remain charged after errors
and timeouts. Service usage/invoice cost is unknown: this is an admission ceiling
with conservative overhead, not a billing guarantee. Workflow reruns are disabled;
a new explicitly authorized dispatch starts a new scope.

The transport and Google wire schema are tested with mocks. **No live Vertex
evaluation verified this change.** Check service availability, IAM and regional
support on the first manual run. Pricing checked 2026-10-29: Flash-Lite 2.5 text
input/output are USD 0.10/0.40 per million tokens, below Flash-Lite 3.1's
USD 0.25/1.50. Review the pinned model and reservation before changing tariffs.

## Later: simulated users

`evals/adk/personas/customer_service.scenarios.json` contains valid ADK
ConversationScenario scaffolds for order status, refunds over EUR 100 and prompt
injection using the EVALUATOR persona. They are schema-tested, but excluded from
evalsets, CI and the manual judge. No simulator model is enabled. Activation needs
its own budget and a multi-turn customer agent; today's advice interface is one turn.

## Google references checked 2026-10-29

The implementation was checked against pinned ADK 2.13.0 and these official docs:

- [ADK evaluation](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/evaluate/)
- [ADK criteria](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/evaluate/criteria/)
- [ADK user simulation](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/evaluate/user-sim/)
- [Vertex evaluation overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/models/evaluation-overview)
- [Pointwise API](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/projects.locations/evaluateInstances)
- [Judge configuration](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/models/configure-judge-model)
- [Google Cloud model pricing](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing)

# Local health and evaluation evidence

Open [Health & evals](http://localhost:8010/health) from the delivery, restaurant or
inventory workspace. The category tally and recent-run pattern follows the
Scrapmarket health page; this implementation uses local files and probes, with
no Firestore, cloud deployment or model requests.

## Collect evidence

Start the stack with `make up`. Then, from Bash:

```bash
make health
```

This builds a disposable checker container, runs the full pytest suite against
`delivery_test`, runs Ruff and mypy, evaluates twelve role scenarios twice, and
evaluates the fixed recovery-judge rules baseline. It does not restart the running
app or its database/Redis dependencies.
The checker forces `LLM_PROVIDER=disabled`; its evaluation command never accepts a
cloud endpoint. It requires a configured `delivery_test` URL and also binds the
subprocesses' default database to that test database. A nonzero test/check result
makes the command fail while preserving
the available evidence. Source edits during the check also make it fail.

`make test` also records case-level test results. GitHub CI uses the same local
runner and uploads its safe JSON reports even on failure. CI artifacts are not
automatically downloaded into the local dashboard.

The checker image is Python-only. JavaScript syntax is explicitly **unavailable**
there when Node is absent; this is not counted as a pass and does not fail the
Python check command. With Node available the runner checks every first-party
`web/*.js` file. A local Bash syntax check is also available:

```bash
node --check web/health.js
```

`DOCKER` can override the Docker executable, for example `make DOCKER=docker.exe
health` in a Bash environment that needs the Windows executable.

## What the page shows

- **Test catalogue:** all collected parameter cases, explicit categories, search,
  result and integration filters. Expand a file, then a check for its description,
  source line, original case ID, duration and failing phase. Descriptions come from
  test docstrings or names; they are not generated assertions about test coverage.
- **Role scenarios:** inventory, restaurant, dispatcher and courier scorecards,
  failed-case/role filters, expandable expected/actual criteria, repetition numbers
  and bounded source event trails. `make eval-agents` runs only these scenarios.
  All 49 declared criteria are scored; a correct business refusal can be a pass.
  See [scenario contracts, scoring and reproducibility](AGENT-EVALS.md).
- **Capability regressions:** selected regressions for queue resilience, coordination,
  memory isolation, budget admission, disrupted-city scenarios and replay. Each
  card links to its cases and states its limits. These groups overlap and must
  not be added into a second test total.
- **Rules baseline:** the six fixed recovery-judge cases, with expected and actual
  decisions and local latency. The rules oracle is compared with itself. This
  checks the evaluation harness, not model quality, live latency or model cost.
- **City health:** read-only Postgres/PostGIS and Redis probes, selected-run queue
  counts, expired leases, dead letters, retries, durable run budgets and model/search
  reservations. Reservations are not actual provider usage or a monetary estimate.
  Historical failed scenarios stay visible. Business failures are distinct from
  infrastructure failure.
- **Run history:** up to 12 finished receipts, retaining their original scope,
  source and outcomes. Invalid receipts are counted as unreadable, not passed.

The page refreshes every 30 seconds while visible. The refresh button reads
existing results; it cannot execute tests or accept shell arguments. Open test
details remain expanded as results refresh. Dates use Europe/Madrid.

## Evidence boundaries

The opt-in `delivery.health_report` pytest plugin records collection and all
setup/call/teardown outcomes. A teardown failure overrides a successful call.
Skipped, expected-failure, unexpected-pass, unrun and filtered cases stay distinct.
Collection-only and interrupted runs cannot be reported as a full passing suite.
Missing evidence is unknown, with no fallback to the old headline of 307 tests.

A deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint covers source, tests, SQL, agent/config files,
web assets, scripts, fixed data including the compressed road graph, the tested
gateway source, dependency files, Dockerfile, Makefile and CI workflow. The reader
compares it with the running app's copy of those files. Host edits need a rebuilt
app to appear in that comparison. A base Git revision is supplementary metadata;
it does not replace the fingerprint for a dirty working tree.

Results older than 24 hours, changed sources, and edits during a check are marked
explicitly. Reports use atomic replacement. Failed refreshes remove current/green
claims and retain the catalogue only as historical evidence.

Reports live in ignored `artifacts/health/`. They contain test identifiers,
docstrings, statuses and timings, not captured stdout, tracebacks, failure messages,
fixture representations, environment variables, database URLs or agent memories.
Use descriptive explicit IDs for parametrized inputs rather than embedding long
payloads or credentials in case names. These files are local development receipts,
not signed attestations or a sandbox against a hostile host operator.

Role receipts additionally retain typed criterion observations and fixture-only
event metadata. Two repeated runs retain all observations: failures and omissions
cannot be erased by a later pass. The reader recomputes scores from the versioned
manifest. Source, input-configuration and business-outcome hashes make drift visible.

The read-only `/api/health/evidence` and `/api/health/runtime` endpoints are for the
trusted local operator. They use the same local-host gate as supply endpoints.
They do not grant an agent any new tool or memory access.

## Extend the dashboard

`config/health-categories.json` is the reviewed taxonomy. Give each new test file
one primary category; unmatched files appear under **Needs classification**.
Capability selectors can reference a whole test file or an exact test function;
parameter variants are included automatically. A missing selector is a visible
measurement gap. Category membership is not a percentage of requirements covered.

Live-model quality/cost, held-out scenario results, architecture comparisons,
semantic recall and long-term memory summaries remain **not measured**. Add them
with versioned fixtures, actual results, source/model versions, budget accounting
and explicit measurement scope rather than reusing the regression pass rate.

## Verification

Current role-evaluation verification (2026-10-28): 392 tests passed, Ruff and mypy
(40 source modules) passed, and the two-run seed-731 role battery matched at 12/12
cases and 49/49 criteria. All four roles scored 100% on these fixed criteria.
Browser checks covered unmeasured/running receipts, role and failed-case filters,
criterion/event repetition provenance and expanded details surviving refresh.
No console errors or horizontal page overflow; app/Postgres/Redis stayed running.
See [role evaluation receipt](evidence/agent-scenarios-local.json). The earlier
353-test dashboard baseline below is retained as historical evidence.

Verified locally on 2026-10-28: 353 tests passed, including 46 reporting/health
checks. Ruff and mypy (38 source modules) passed. The dashboard indexed 36 test
files into ten categories with no unclassified file or missing capability selector.
All six fixed offline judge cases passed, with zero model decisions or tokens.
The running app's fingerprint matched every current receipt.

Browser checks covered missing/collection evidence, source changes in history,
search and category filters, case IDs, persistent expanded inspection, capability
drill-down (15 memory cases), real historical dead-letter diagnostics, and the
explicit unmeasured model/architecture sections. Both local service probes passed;
Postgres and Redis identities/start times were unchanged by the check command.
Host JavaScript syntax passed; browser console errors and horizontal overflow were
zero at the default viewport. The Python-only checker correctly marked its missing
Node check unavailable. The [local receipt](evidence/local-health.json) records the
results and limitations.

# Local Bakiano sample and execution policy

Decision: 2026-10-23. Build and polish locally. GCP portability remains optional
future work, not a prerequisite or an always-on demo environment.

## Current frozen sample

Requested ten daily buckets: **2026-10-14 through 2026-10-23 inclusive**. Today minus
ten through today would contain eleven dates (October 13-23); ten dates including
today begin October 14.

The local private package contains **2,008 product observations** across nine
available dates, October 14-22. October 23 had no matching observations at extraction
time and remains explicitly missing. This is a frozen extraction, not a completeness
claim about later warehouse updates. No scheduled refresh or live query is required.

Sources: Gama, Central Madeirense and Plazas (supermarkets); Daka and EPA (retail).
Select at most 50 stable source listing identities per vendor across the whole
window, rather than a different random assortment every day. Individual days can
contain fewer than 50 observations per vendor. This sample is not representative
of the full assortment, market or sales. Stock, shipments and demand remain simulated.

Only vendors confirmed as USD in Bakiano's registry are selected. Preserve source
listing IDs, observed prices rounded to cents, categories/URLs where available and
missing values. The daily bucket uses warehouse ingestion date; collection timestamps
are retained in the manifest. A listing is not proof of real store availability.

Files live in ignored `data/local/bakiano/`: manifest plus one catalogue per available
day. Date entries include per-source counts and content hashes. Missing days have no
catalogue file. Never forward-fill prices or relabel old products as new observations.
The public [coverage receipt](bakiano-sample-coverage.json) contains counts only.

## Use entirely offline

The local app exposes date selection at `/lab`. Each fictional store binds to one
source catalogue; product observations remain separate from generated stock. Missing
dates cannot start runs. The manifest and chosen snapshot hash are checked before use.

```sh
docker compose up -d --build --wait
docker compose exec -T app delivery lab-demo --sample-date 2026-10-22
```

Compose mounts `data/local/` read-only and excludes it from the image build context.
The private sample is also excluded from Git. The committed synthetic fixture runs
when no private package exists. Default Compose services do not receive `.env`
credentials, remote model calls are disabled, and host settings do not implicitly
load `.env`. Explicit process environment settings remain an opt-in developer interface.

No local runtime command reads Bakiano's warehouse, starts GCP infrastructure or
refreshes the sample. Existing provider adapters are retained as optional code, not
activated by ordinary local startup.

## Optional one-time acquisition

The exporter is a separate opt-in preparation tool. It needs an authenticated
BigQuery CLI only on the machine fetching the sample, not in the application image.
It reads only selected catalogue columns for five sources and explicit date
partitions. It never modifies Bakiano tables, triggers collectors or deploys services.
The query is dry-run first and capped at 1 GiB billed bytes; LIMIT alone is not a
scan-cost control. Actual extraction processed 202,235,905 bytes, below the cap.

```sh
python scripts/export_bakiano_sample.py --project PROJECT_ID --start 2026-10-14 --end 2026-10-23
python scripts/export_bakiano_sample.py --project PROJECT_ID --start 2026-10-14 --end 2026-10-23 --execute
```

The first command only validates the query. Existing output directories are never
overwritten. For a later refresh, use `--output` with a new directory, verify its
manifest, then deliberately select/install that package. For a failed result download,
`--resume-job` retrieves a matching completed query's temporary result table without
executing the query again, while it remains available. The CLI prints its job ID
before downloading and forces UTF-8 to preserve Spanish names on Windows.

Keep extraction credentials outside datasets, prompts, event payloads and traces.
Only the root extraction process handles them; delegated code/documentation work
uses synthetic records and no private sample access.

# M2 first slice: inventory recovery

Implemented 2026-10-23. This is a first vertical slice, not completion of every M2 target.

## What runs

- A generated, hash-versioned 100-node (10×10), 360-edge directed fictional city: three supermarkets,
  two retail stores, depot, supplier, fuel and charging locations. Coordinates are
  fictional metres. Roads are an inspectable fixture; routing traffic/couriers over
  it is later work.
- A validated catalogue contract and read-only CSV adapter for Bakiano collector
  exports with explicitly confirmed USD prices. Identity, dates, unknown category
  and source provenance are preserved. Domain separates grocery and retail stock.
- Five committed synthetic products for an offline demo. Ten real Daka listings
  were imported from the local Bakiano export dated 2026-04-05 into an ignored local
  snapshot. These are historical observed listings, not current stock or prices.
- Versioned, checksum-checked additive SQL migrations; per-run stock, baskets,
  shipments and movement ledger. Existing Madrid state is separate from lab runs.
- Atomic last-unit reservation, idempotent receipt/release, simulation-time expiry,
  confirmed-stock availability and forecast incoming supply.

## Scenario evidence

1. Two one-unit baskets target one confirmed unit at the same store.
2. A subprocess claims the first event, writes a reservation inside its transaction
   and abruptly exits with code 73 before commit/ACK. Its database writes, decision
   and outgoing messages roll back; the durable leased event remains.
3. The controller waits for the real wall-clock lease expiry. A replacement worker
   reclaims the event on attempt two. Basket A reserves; basket B is rejected.
4. At simulation second 120, replenishment moves from second 300 to second 900.
   At the original ETA, no incoming units are sellable.
5. At second 600 the unused reservation expires. At second 900 five units arrive,
   leaving six confirmed available units. No collection or sale is simulated here.

The fixed demo uses deterministic queue tie-breaking. A separate two-thread
Postgres integration test creates actual concurrent last-unit contention and
asserts exactly one winner. Another subprocess test exits after commit (code 74)
and proves the ACK and stock effect survive. A two-delay regression proves obsolete
receipt events cannot create stock before the latest ETA.

Snapshots use repeatable-read transactions. Every scenario checkpoint checks ledger
conservation and nonnegative availability. Evidence JSON includes city/catalogue
hashes, stock versions, event lineage/attempts, decisions, movements and checkpoints.
These are captured inspection checkpoints, not yet a full replay/import engine.

## Verification

- Initial slice: 25 tests passed against dedicated Postgres `delivery_test`, including the existing
  Madrid regression suite, real process crashes and the new API contracts.
- Ruff and mypy passed. One existing upstream Starlette TestClient deprecation
  warning remains.
- Both synthetic and imported-Bakiano CLI runs completed with exit-73 recovery and
  passing stock invariants. Generated artifacts stay in ignored `artifacts/`.
- `scripts/lab_browser_smoke.py` exercises actual scenario start, crash/race/delay
  checkpoints, store selection and desktop/mobile layout. Run with the separately
  installed Playwright dependency documented for browser checks.
  Chrome checks passed at 1440x1100 and 390x844 with no page errors or mobile overflow.

The shared-agent extension now passes 67 tests, Ruff, mypy and the dated-sample
browser check. See [foundation verification](AGENT-FOUNDATION.md).

## Limits and next boundary

The agent currently uses deterministic queue handlers and inventory tools, not a
GCP-deployed reasoning framework. Role-isolated database credentials and the shared inventory runtime are now implemented;
see [foundation verification](AGENT-FOUNDATION.md). pgvector,
model-assisted inventory judgment, full baskets/fulfillment, cancellation events,
expiry scheduling for arbitrary orders and a larger catalogue are subsequent work.
The current fixture schedules expiry for its known winning basket explicitly.

The controller lives in the local API background task or CLI. Worker-process crashes
are recovered; controller/API restarts do not resume a running scenario. Do not claim
controller crash recovery. An interrupted run stays inspectable; use the CLI for a
fresh run. Durable supervision/resumption belongs in the shared runtime work.

No model calls, cloud deployment, live supplier requests or real financial operations
are used. No credentials or private catalogue rows were committed.
